Problems solved by arbitrary-order decoding are largely a subset of those solved by autoregressive-order decoding in the Pass@ solution-coverage analysis (Figure 4)
The paper identifies entropy degradation at logical-fork tokens as a mechanism by which arbitrary-order decoding bypasses hard decisions and narrows exploration (Figure 7)
JustGRPO reaches 89.1% GSM8K accuracy with standard GRPO on LLaDA-Instruct while avoiding diffusion-specific RL adaptations (Table 1)
JustGRPO-trained models remain compatible with parallel decoding, with larger accuracy gains at higher parallel token counts than the original instruct model (Figure 8)

71132.text: The diffusion sampler attains delta-error in polylog(1/delta) steps given sufficiently accurate score estimates, improving the dependence on accuracy over prior high-accuracy samplers (Theorem 4.3)
Under minimal data assumptions, the diffusion sampling complexity is stated as Õ(d polylog(1/delta)), where d is the data dimension (Theorem 4.3)
When the data distribution has intrinsic dimension d*, the complexity reduces to Õ(d* polylog(1/delta)) (Corollary 4.4)
Under a non-uniform Lipschitz condition, the diffusion sampling complexity is refined to Õ(sqrt(dL) polylog(1/delta)) (Theorem 4.9)
The same framework yields a polylog(1/delta)-accuracy sampler for log-concave and more general isoperimetric distributions using first-order gradient queries (Section 5)

71065.text: The paper constructs MBPP-Honeypot, a coding reward-hacking setting where hardcoding hidden tests naturally induces deceptive behavior during RLVR (Section 4.1)
Training against a deception detector produces four observed policy outcomes: honesty, blatant deception, obfuscated activations, and obfuscated policies (Table 1)
Insufficient KL regularization and detector penalty lead models to evade probes through obfuscated activations or obfuscated policies (Figure 2)
Passing gradients directly through the detector increases obfuscated activations and is recommended against by the authors (Figure 4)
Moderately high KL and high detector penalty can produce honest policies with task capability comparable to the best honest no-code-length-penalty policy (Figure 5)

71049.text: Motive computes motion-specific influence by detecting motion, forming motion-magnitude patches, and applying motion masks to gradient-based data attribution (Figure 1)
Motive-selected fine-tuning data improves VBench motion smoothness and dynamic degree compared with random and baseline data-selection methods (Table 1)
Human pairwise evaluation reports a 74.1% preference win rate for Motive-selected fine-tuning over the pretrained base model (Table 2)
Frame-length normalization prevents attribution rankings from being biased toward longer clips and yields more coherent top-ranked motion samples (Figure 4)
Motive's influence scores are not merely selecting high-motion clips; influential clips are those predicted to improve target motion dynamics (Figure 6)

bA6BgSbaUi.text: GPT-style transformers trained on uniform random data show an empirical memorization-capacity plateau of about 3.6 bits per parameter (Figure 1)
Capacity estimates across model widths and depths support a roughly linear bits-per-parameter scaling law, with bfloat16 to float32 increasing capacity only modestly (Table 1)
On text data, unintended memorization rises with model size but decreases once models begin generalizing relative to an oracle reference model (Figure 2)
Double descent begins when dataset information content exceeds estimated model capacity in both synthetic bitstrings and text experiments (Figures 3 and 4)
The paper derives and evaluates scaling-law predictions for membership inference as a function of model capacity and dataset size (Figure 7)

Finite-sample covariance effects renormalize the effective noise scale in the expected linear denoiser, causing overshrinkage of low-variance directions (Figure 2)
The denoiser-variance theory predicts anisotropic, location-dependent cross-split deviations that decay with dataset size (Result 4.2)
The sampling-map analysis gives deterministic-equivalence formulas for expectation and variance over full diffusion trajectories (Results 5.1 and 5.2)
UNet and DiT experiments validate the theory's predictions about consistency, overshrinkage, and eigenmode-dependent deviations in the non-memorization regime (Figure 5)

The end-to-end grokking result is extended from the zero-teacher setting to realizable ridge regression with arbitrary realizable teacher functions (Theorem 4.2)
Separate theorems decompose grokking into training-loss convergence, poor generalization during overfitting, and eventual generalization (Theorems 4.4-4.6)
Decreasing weight decay and sample size can amplify grokking time in ridge-regression simulations, matching the paper's quantitative hyperparameter predictions (Figure 2)
Two-layer ReLU experiments qualitatively reproduce the predicted grokking-time dependence on hyperparameters beyond the linear setting (Figures 3 and 4)

Argument switching, biased fact inconsistency, answer flipping, and other patterns occur among IPHR pairs classified as unfaithful (Figure 3)
Thinking and non-thinking frontier models both exhibit unfaithful illogical shortcuts on hard math problems, though rates vary by model (Figure 5)

Synthetic random-token inputs overestimate speculative-decoding throughput by an average of 23% compared with SPEED-Bench real-data throughput workloads (Figure 6)

The benchmark is partitioned into LLM-only, toolkit-only, and compositional-agent parts with different interaction sparsity and long-tail reuse patterns (Figure 3)
Leaderboard results show content-aware semantic matching and tuned embedding recommenders outperform ID-centric methods in the sparse Parts II and III settings (Table 2)

A semantic compatibility matrix is used to avoid implausible event co-occurrences during mixture synthesis (Figure 5)
Enforcing semantic-consistency constraints yields consistent gains over random mixtures built from the same purified single-event sources (Table 3)
Hive-trained AudioSep and FlowSep are compared against original checkpoints and SAM-Audio on the Hive test set and third-party out-of-distribution benchmarks (Tables 4 and 5)
Paired co-occurrence/decorrelation tests show Hive training reduces shortcut reliance while controlling target identity, source count, and SNR (Table 6)

The benchmark includes both declarative/procedural memory and explicit/implicit feedback categories absent from prior memory benchmarks (Table 1)
Off-policy results show that advanced memory systems such as A-Mem, Mem0, and MemoryOS do not consistently outperform simpler RAG baselines (Figure 2)

Compared with prior multilingual document benchmarks, MORE has broader language coverage and annotation coverage for structural document elements (Table 3)

Training-inference alignment follows when the same segmented execution semantics and truncated objective are used for training and inference (Corollary 3.4)
The architecture uses head- and layer-sparse long-range retrieval with carried KV tails and forward-only retrieved prefixes (Figure 3)
The method achieves comparable LongBench-E performance while lowering prefill memory and latency relative to full-context attention and other efficient baselines (Table 1)

R4T improves weakly supervised compositional retrieval on Polyvore relative to no-fan-out, zero-shot fan-out, and best-of-N baselines (Table 2).

WTziQZdpTV.text: RepoNavigator equips an LLM agent with a single execution-aware jump tool backed by symbol resolution from a language server (Figure 1; Section 3.3).
RepoNavigator is trained with GRPO using a hybrid reward combining localization Dice with tool-use success (Section 3.4).

RL-trained RepoNavigator improves function-level and file-level localization on SWE-bench_Verified over same-size baselines, with 7B models outperforming 14B baselines and 14B models surpassing 32B competitors (Table 1).
RepoNavigator also achieves state-of-the-art localization performance on SWE-bench_Pro across compared agent pipelines (Table 2).
Increasing the allowed number of jump-tool calls improves localization performance before and after RL training, supporting a scaling law of tool-calling (Figure 4).
Substituting RepoNavigator localization into an Agentless repair pipeline improves downstream SWE-bench_Verified issue resolution (Table 3).

TbUbv5zqTF.text: SALAAD induces sparse-plus-low-rank structure during training via block-wise ADMM-style updates and an adaptive I-controller for rank and sparsity thresholds (Algorithm 1; Section 4).
Across LLaMA-based model scales, SALAAD structured surrogate models match or outperform representative low-rank and sparse baselines in perplexity under comparable parameter budgets (Table 1).
Homomorphic Parameter Allocation enables a single SALAAD-trained checkpoint to trade parameter budget for perplexity smoothly at deployment time (Figure 3; Figure 8).
A SALAAD-compressed 1B model with 646M parameters achieves downstream zero-shot accuracy comparable to the vanilla 1B model across MMLU, ARC-C, COPA, HellaSwag, BoolQ, and PIQA (Table 2).
Ablations show that adaptive regularization and homomorphic allocation improve the 350M model's perplexity/parameter trade-off (Table 3; Figure 4).

Li5ki5Dopo.text: Ambient Dataloops iteratively trains a diffusion model on a noisy dataset and uses posterior sampling to refine that same dataset for subsequent loops (Figure 2; Algorithm 1).
On CIFAR-10 with 90% corrupted and 10% clean data, one Ambient Dataloops iteration improves unconditional and conditional generation metrics over Ambient Diffusion Omni and other baselines (Table 1).
The denoising rate per loop has a non-monotonic effect, with too-fast or too-slow progress degrading FID and an over-denoising 'madness regime' hurting performance (Figure 3; Table 3).
Ambient Dataloops improves COCO zero-shot text-to-image generation and GenEval scores relative to using the initial synthetic dataset as clean (Table 2).
In de novo protein backbone design, one Ambient Dataloops iteration produces a new Pareto point with a 14.3% diversity increase for a 0.2% designability decrease (Figure 4).
The paper provides theoretical justification that idealized dataset refinement can reduce estimation error after looping (Section 4; Appendix A).

3ExTD9F0u1.text: TFRBench introduces a reasoning-aware forecasting benchmark that evaluates cross-channel dependencies, trends, and external-event reasoning alongside numerical forecasts (Figure 1; Table 1).
TFRBench constructs reference reasoning with a multi-agent generate-verify-refine loop that filters traces by verifier score and MASE improvement over a naive baseline (Figure 2; Algorithm 1).
The benchmark spans ten datasets across Energy, Sales, Web/CloudOps, Transportation, and Finance domains (Table 2).
LLM-as-a-Judge reasoning scores are strongly correlated with forecasting accuracy, with higher reasoning quality corresponding to lower MASE (Figure 5).
Prompting models with verified reasoning traces improves success rates over direct prompting, including Solar from 30.7% to 70.4% and Hierarchical Sales from 54.7% to 78.5% (Figure 6).
Off-the-shelf LLMs show domain-dependent reasoning failures, including narrative bias in stochastic finance settings despite gains in pattern-rich domains (Table 3; Figure 4).

oBgLvd5YC6.text: SimpleMem uses a three-stage memory pipeline: semantic structured compression, online semantic synthesis, and intent-aware retrieval planning (Figure 2).
On LoCoMo with high-capability backends, SimpleMem achieves a superior F1/token-cost trade-off over baseline memory systems (Figure 1; Table 1).
On LongMemEval-S, SimpleMem obtains the best overall performance while maintaining balanced sub-task accuracy (Table 2).
SimpleMem remains effective with small models, with 1.5B/3B backends often outperforming larger models using baseline memory systems (Table 3).
On LoCoMo-10 with GPT-4.1-mini, SimpleMem reduces construction and retrieval time versus graph- or summary-based baselines while achieving the highest average F1 (Table 4).
Ablations show that semantic structured compression, online synthesis, and intent-aware retrieval planning each contribute materially to reasoning performance (Table 5).

DVHpvumD60.text: WarmServe uses workload forecasting, model placement, proactive GPU prewarming, KV-cache reservation, and GPU memory switching for multi-LLM serving (Figure 3; Section 3).
Real-world LLM request peaks in 5-minute windows are predictable enough for prewarming, with reported average peak-load relative error of 7.3% on AzureConv (Figure 2; Section 3.1).
Successful prewarming substantially reduces model TTFT compared with loading weights on demand (Table 2).
WarmServe reduces tail TTFT by up to 50.8x compared with autoscaling-based systems in end-to-end experiments (Figure 4).
Ablations show that removing model prewarming, placement, or proactive prewarming sharply reduces the fraction of requests meeting the 100 ms TTFT threshold (Figure 5).
In a 512-GPU simulation, WarmServe maintains lower P99 TTFT than compared multi-LLM serving systems (Table 3).

PLT2FKIs2c.text: LightYourFace-160K provides 160,000 paired before/after face fill-light examples generated with a physically consistent renderer and six-dimensional disk-area-light controls (Section 3).
PALP embeds the 6D physical lighting parameters into diffusion-compatible conditioning tokens using an auxiliary planar-light reconstruction objective (Section 3).
FiLitDiff is a one-step diffusion model conditioned on physically grounded lighting codes for controllable face fill-light enhancement (Section 3).
FiLitDiff achieves strong full-reference metrics and perceptual quality on LYF-Val while preserving scene/background illumination (Table 1; Figure 6).
FiLitDiff achieves strong results on LYF-EditVal for prompt/edit-style fill-light enhancement relative to representative relighting and editing baselines (Table 2; Figure 7).

QgoRoKIEEr.text: The paper identifies Posterior Progressive Concentration, where the effective posterior support shrinks from a global manifold to a local neighborhood as signal-to-noise ratio increases (Figure 1).
GoldDiff dynamically selects a time-aware golden subset to decouple analytical diffusion inference complexity from full dataset size (Section 3; Table 1).
GoldDiff matches or exceeds full-scan analytical denoiser quality while achieving large per-step speedups and lower memory on AFHQ and related image datasets (Table 2).
GoldDiff is reported as the first analytical diffusion method scaled successfully to ImageNet-1K in unconditional and conditional settings (Table 3).
GoldDiff's sparse approximation is compatible with neural denoisers and improves matching to EDM-VP/EDM-VE outputs over PCA baselines (Table 4).
Ablations show coarse candidate set size and golden subset size control the quality-efficiency trade-off (Figure 6).

NMMmwSbzRx.text: Stream RAG issues tool queries in parallel with incoming user speech to reduce user-perceived latency in speech-in speech-out dialogue systems (Figure 1; Figure 3).
The paper introduces AudioCRAG by converting CRAG question-answer tasks into speech form, including a human-recorded subset of 618 spoken queries (Section 4.1).
Tool integration improves factual QA accuracy for speech-in speech-out systems but increases first-token latency by about 2.3x in the open-book setting (Table 1; Table 3).
Model-triggered Stream RAG improves Qwen2.5-7B AudioCRAG accuracy from 11.1% closed-book to 34.2% absolute while reducing tool-use latency by about 20% (Table 1).
Latency breakdowns show Stream RAG reduces P50 first-token latency and tool-result latency relative to open-book tool use (Table 3).
Negative sampling during model-triggered Stream RAG post-training improves robustness to intermediate query-prediction errors (Table 5).

aIFgQusnPy.text: The paper frames Diffusion Bridge and Flow Matching in a shared stochastic optimal control/optimal transport framework (Section 4).
Theoretical analysis shows the Diffusion Bridge cost function is lower than Flow Matching under the paper's formulation, implying more stable trajectories (Proposition 4.1; Theorem 4.2).
Under a shared Transformer architecture, Diffusion Bridge outperforms Flow Matching across image restoration and translation tasks (Table 1; Figure 2).
Diffusion Bridge remains stronger than Flow Matching as inpainting mask size increases, indicating better robustness under harder transformations (Table 2; Figure 3a).
Flow Matching degrades more steeply than Diffusion Bridge when training data size is reduced (Figure 3b; Table 7).
Using the same network input conditions does not eliminate the performance gap between Flow Matching and Diffusion Bridge (Table 4).

Oz335dV48X.text: DFlash uses a lightweight block diffusion draft model to generate speculative draft tokens in parallel, conditioned on hidden features extracted from the target LLM (Figure 2).
On Qwen3 models with thinking disabled, DFlash consistently outperforms EAGLE-3 and reaches about 4.9x average greedy-decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding (Table 1).
With thinking mode enabled, DFlash maintains high acceptance length and roughly 4.5x speedups on reasoning-model settings (Table 2).
On SGLang with the FA4 backend, DFlash provides throughput speedups across Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct up to 5.1x (Table 3).
Long-context fine-tuning preserves or improves DFlash acceptance length as LongBench context length increases beyond 4K (Table 4).
Ablations show that draft depth, number of target hidden features, block-size choice, and KV injection all materially affect DFlash acceptance length and speedup (Table 6; Table 7; Table 8; Table 9).

5f0gw9YpZC.text: GUDA approximates leave-one-group-out counterfactual diffusion models by unlearning each group from a shared full-data model, then scores group influence by ELBO differences (Figure 1; Algorithm 1).
On CIFAR-10 group attribution, GUDA achieves the best or tied-best head-focused attribution metrics while reducing wall-clock cost versus LOGO retraining (Table 1).
On UnlearnCanvas artistic style attribution, GUDA outperforms semantic similarity and gradient/instance-level baselines on head-identification metrics (Table 2; Figure 2).
GUDA's weighted style-selection anchor strategy improves UnlearnCanvas attribution over simpler anchor alternatives (Table 3).
Detailed cost analysis reports about 100x speedup over LOGOA on CIFAR-10 and 5.9x speedup over LOGOA on UnlearnCanvas (Table 11; Table 12).
GUDA remains robust under a 5% noisy group partition on CIFAR-10 relative to compared attribution baselines (Table 16).

TBaUfO9znF.text: The paper uses a controlled synthetic reasoning framework with explicit dependency graphs, contextual templates, and process-verified evaluation (Figure 2).

RL yields extrapolative pass@128 gains only when the post-training tasks sit near the model's edge of competence; gains vanish when tasks are already covered or too far out-of-distribution (Figure 1; Figure 3).
Contextual generalization requires minimal but nonzero pre-training exposure to long-tail contexts; exposure of at least about 1% enables RL to reinforce transfer (Figure 1; Figure 4).
Mid-training plus RL outperforms RL alone on OOD-hard reasoning under fixed compute, with reported +10.8% gains (Figure 1; Figure 6).
Process-aware reward compositions reduce shortcut exploitation and improve reasoning performance relative to pure outcome rewards (Figure 7).
Training dynamics show reward stagnates when RL data are too easy or too hard, but improves when tasks are calibrated to the edge of competence (Figure 11).

Wfe1iJocjF.text: FlashOptim combines improved master-weight splitting with companded 8-bit optimizer-state quantization to reduce parameter-associated optimizer memory (Section 3).
FlashOptim reduces AdamW training memory from 16 to 7 bytes per parameter, or 5 bytes with gradient release (Table 1).
For Llama-3.1-8B finetuning, FlashOptim reduces peak memory from 175 GiB to 113 GiB by compressing parameters and optimizer states (Figure 1; Table 4).
FlashOptim variants match reference optimizer training-loss trajectories in GPT-2 pretraining and ResNet-50 image classification (Figure 2).
FlashOptim matches reference scores on ResNet-50 validation accuracy, Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K finetuning, and GPT-2 in-context learning benchmarks (Table 2; Table 3).
ULP-based weight splitting lowers FP32 reconstruction error and companding prevents quantized AdamW training divergence compared with linear optimizer-state quantization (Figure 3; Figure 5).

a3GdvuPItd.text: The paper casts dataset pruning as a graph problem with node weights for intrinsic importance and edge weights for extrinsic diversity/interaction, yielding a Maximum Weight Clique formulation (Section 3.3).
Under mild conditions, the unified objective becomes submodular and admits a greedy approximation guarantee (Section 3.6; Appendix F).
UGIES outperforms state-of-the-art dataset pruning methods on CIFAR-10/100 with ResNet-18 (Table 1).
On ImageNet-1K, UGIES achieves lossless or better-than-lossless pruning with ResNet-50 and Swin-T at moderate pruning ratios (Table 2).
With ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1K at a 50% pruning ratio, UGIES reaches the same accuracy while saving 43.2% total training cost (Table 3).
Ablations show combining intrinsic and extrinsic importance terms outperforms using either component alone across pruning ratios (Table 4).

prvGhNz39e.text: SCALE combines column-wise gradient normalization with first-order momentum only on the LM output layer (Algorithm 1; Section 3).
Column-wise gradient normalization is faster than singular-value normalization and avoids the unstable LM-head gradient spikes observed with row-wise normalization (Table 1; Figure 3).
Last-layer-only momentum targets the layer with the largest stochastic-gradient variance while adding minimal optimizer-state memory (Figure 4).
Across LLaMA 60M-1B pretraining on C4, SCALE matches or exceeds Adam-like performance while using about 35-45% of Adam's total memory (Table 5; Figure 1).
For LLaMA 7B pretraining, SCALE outperforms APOLLO and Muon in both perplexity and memory consumption (Table 6).
SCALE remains stable when training a 7B LLaMA on C4 up to 100B tokens, reaching final evaluation perplexity 9.32 (Figure 5).

3qX5RS8kpJ.text: DVPD uses a dual-branch predictive/diffusion architecture that treats spectrograms as both acoustic frequency-domain structures and visual textures (Figure 1; Figure 2).
The FANC encoder preserves low-frequency harmonics while pruning high-frequency redundancy using frequency-adaptive non-uniform compression (Section 3.3).
DVPD attains state-of-the-art speech enhancement quality on WSJ0-UNI while using 35% of PGUSE parameters and 40% of PGUSE inference MACs (Table 1).
Training only on WSJ0-UNI, DVPD generalizes across multiple out-of-distribution speech enhancement benchmarks better than compared predictive and diffusion baselines (Figure 5).
DVPD improves over compared methods on VBDMD speech denoising and VBDMD-SR speech super-resolution evaluations (Table 2; Table 3).
Ablations show that FANC, the frequency-aware interaction module, LISA, and the TLB strategy each contribute to DVPD performance (Table 4; Table 5).

tI5CFbRhmV.text: Traditional code complexity metrics show no stable correlation with LLM task performance after controlling for code length (Table 1).
LM-CC builds a hierarchical semantic decomposition from token-entropy signals and syntactic delimiters to estimate model-perceived code complexity (Figure 2; Algorithm 1).
LM-CC achieves statistically significant partial Spearman correlations with pass@1 across program repair, code translation, and execution reasoning while controlling for code length (Table 2).
Semantics-preserving rewrites that reduce LM-CC improve LLM task performance, with reported gains up to 20.9% (Table 3).
LM-CC's correlation advantage generalizes to GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3.5-122B settings (Table 4).
Ablations show that both entropy-based decomposition and syntactic delimiter structure contribute to LM-CC's stable correlations (Table 5; Figure 3).

hJnZKtsDbe.text: AgentExpt builds a resource knowledge base linking 108,825 accepted papers to the baselines and datasets they used, covering about 85% of such resources in top AI conferences over the past five years (Section 3.1).
The collective perception-enhanced retriever represents each baseline or dataset by combining self-descriptions with aggregated citation contexts before embedding retrieval (Section 3.2).
The reasoning-augmented reranker uses baseline-dataset interaction chains to produce interpretable justifications and refined rankings (Section 3.3).
AgentExpt improves over the strongest prior competitor by average gains of +5.85% Recall@20, +8.30% HitRate@5, and +7.90% HitRate@10 (Table 2).

fl93PQfTT6.text: The paper identifies three DLLM-specific PTQ issues: timestep-dependent token distributions, iterative quantization-error accumulation, and masked/unmasked feature distribution mismatch (Section 3).
DLLMQuant combines Temporal-Mask Adaptive Sampling, Interaction-Aware Activation Quantization, and Certainty-Guided Quantization for diffusion LLM PTQ (Section 4).
Under W4A4 quantization on LLADA-8B, AWQ suffers about a 16% accuracy drop, motivating DLLM-specific quantization methods (Section 1).
DLLMQuant reports more than a 10-point GSM8K accuracy improvement for LLADA under 4-bit quantization (Table 1).

CzShhpY2qU.text: Agent Primitives instantiates three reusable MAS building blocks: Review, Voting and Selection, and Planning and Execution (Section 3).
The primitives communicate internally through KV-cache states rather than only natural-language message passing (Section 3).
An Organizer agent selects and composes primitives for each query using a lightweight pool of previously successful configurations (Section 3).
Primitive-based MAS improve average accuracy by 12.0-16.5% over single-agent baselines across evaluated tasks (Section 4).
Compared with text-based MAS, Agent Primitives reduce token usage and inference latency by about 3-4x while adding only 1.3-1.6x overhead over single-agent inference (Appendix E).

ycj3XWCh6E.text: The position paper argues that mainstream LLM serving systems still rely on generic policies such as join-shortest-queue or round-robin routing, FIFO scheduling, and LRU KV-cache eviction (Section 2).

The paper identifies dynamically growing KV-cache memory, prefill-decode asymmetry, unknown output lengths, and continuous batching as LLM-specific serving structure ignored by generic heuristics (Section 2).
The paper calls for mathematical workload models that support algorithms with provable performance guarantees across diverse LLM-serving workloads (Section 3).
The paper cites emerging operations-research and ML-systems work as evidence that principled methods can match or exceed heuristic serving performance (Section 4).

FEmXFeqYNZ.text: Success conditioning is proved to exactly solve a trust-region policy optimization problem with a chi-squared divergence constraint whose radius is determined by the data (Section 4.3).
At the optimum, relative policy improvement, chi-squared policy-change magnitude, and action-influence are shown to be exactly equal at every state (Section 4.4).
The analysis characterizes exact success conditioning as a conservative improvement operator that cannot degrade performance or induce dangerous distribution shift (Section 4.3).
The paper analyzes return thresholding as an extension that can amplify improvement but can misalign the learned policy with the true objective (Section 5).

2azIa9tfl3.text: The paper argues that vanilla MLP INR low-frequency bias is a symptom of stable-rank degradation during training rather than an intrinsic architectural limitation (Section 3).
Rank-regulating, near-orthogonal Muon updates improve image overfitting quality across multiple INR architectures compared with Adam (Table 1).
Muon improves sparse-view CT reconstruction quality across multiple INR architectures compared with Adam (Table 4).
The reported improvements extend to natural images, medical images, audio, super-resolution, and novel-view synthesis, with up to about +9 dB PSNR over the same architecture (Tables 1-6).

71171.text: tau^2-Bench introduces a Telecom dual-control domain formalized as a Dec-POMDP in which both the agent and user use tools in a shared dynamic environment (Section 3).
The benchmark includes a compositional task generator that creates diverse, verifiable tasks from atomic components (Section 4).
The user simulator is coupled to the environment through tools and observable state to improve fidelity over passive-user simulations (Section 4).
Agents show substantial performance drops when moving from no-user or single-control settings to the dual-control setting (Section 5).

71030.text: OPUS scores candidate data by projecting optimizer-shaped effective updates onto a target direction from a stable in-distribution proxy (Section 3).
OPUS uses Ghost gradients, CountSketch projections, and Boltzmann sampling with redundancy penalties to make per-iteration selection scalable (Section 3).
The scalable OPUS implementation reports only 4.7% additional compute overhead compared with random sampling (Section 4).
On 30B-token GPT-2 Large/XL pretraining over FineWeb and FineWeb-Edu, OPUS outperforms industrial static filters and online selection baselines (Tables 3-5).
For continued pretraining of Qwen3-8B-Base on SciencePedia, OPUS with 0.5B selected tokens outperforms full training with 3B tokens (Section 4).

71142.text: WeDLM implements diffusion-style parallel decoding entirely with standard causal attention to preserve prefix KV-cache compatibility (Section 3).

Topological Reordering lets each masked position condition on observed tokens under a strict causal mask by moving observed tokens into the physical prefix while preserving logical positions (Section 3).
WeDLM introduces a streaming decoding procedure that commits confident tokens into a growing left-to-right prefix while maintaining a fixed parallel workload (Section 3).

Against vLLM-served autoregressive baselines under matched deployment settings, WeDLM approaches 3x speedups on reasoning benchmarks and up to 10x speedups in low-entropy generation regimes (Section 4).

71034.text: VenusBench-Mobile evaluates mobile GUI agents under realistic user-centric conditions rather than app-centric, task-homogeneous scenarios (Section 2).
The benchmark combines user-intent-driven task design with capability-oriented annotations for fine-grained behavior diagnostics (Section 3).
State-of-the-art mobile GUI agents drop by about 50 average success-rate points on VenusBench-Mobile compared with AndroidWorld (Figure 2).
Diagnostic analysis attributes dominant failures to perception and memory deficiencies that coarse aggregate evaluations obscure (Section 4).
Even the strongest evaluated agents achieve near-zero success under environment variations (Section 4).

71050.text: PhotoAgent formulates autonomous photo editing as long-horizon decision-making with aesthetic-intent reasoning, tree-search planning, and closed-loop execution using memory and visual feedback (Figure 1).
The paper introduces UGC-Edit, a dataset of about 7,000 authentic user-generated photos annotated with human aesthetic scores for training a UGC-specific reward model (Figure 3).
The evaluation includes a real-world autonomous photo-editing test set of 1,017 photos (Section 4).
A 20-participant user study over 27 editing scenarios and 540 votes finds PhotoAgent consistently preferred over baseline methods (Table 2).
PhotoAgent improves both instruction adherence and visual quality compared with baseline editing methods (Section 5).

71069.text: Rex converts explicit Runge-Kutta and stochastic Runge-Kutta schemes into algebraically reversible exponential solvers for diffusion ODEs and SDEs using Lawson methods (Section 3).
The ODE Rex construction inherits arbitrary convergence order and supports reversible adaptive step-size solvers (Section 3.3).
Rex is shown to recover reversible versions of diffusion-model solvers including DDIM, DPM-Solver, and SEEDS-1 (Section 3.3).

Empirically, Rex achieves near-machine-precision reconstruction under exact inversion while remaining competitive on unconditional generation, text-conditioned generation, and image editing (Section 4).
Rex enables accurate likelihood-based Boltzmann sampling on tri-alanine (Appendix G.5).

71038.text: TEDBench is a large-scale, non-redundant protein fold classification benchmark built from TED and Foldseek-clustered AlphaFold structures (Section 3).
The paper shows current protein representation methods on TEDBench either require very large models or fail to deliver strong performance (Section 4).
MiAE uses up to 90% masking with an SE(3)-invariant encoder and lightweight decoder to reconstruct backbone coordinates from latent representations and mask tokens (Section 4).
MiAE scales well and outperforms supervised counterparts and state-of-the-art baselines on TEDBench (Section 5).
The paper evaluates transfer beyond AlphaFold structures on a curated experimental-structure dataset from CATH v4.4 (Section 5).

71037.text: PAR is a multi-scale autoregressive framework for protein backbone generation that performs coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction (Figure 1).
PAR combines multi-scale downsampling, an autoregressive transformer for conditional embeddings, and a flow-based backbone decoder (Figure 1).
PAR addresses autoregressive exposure bias with noisy context learning and scheduled sampling (Section 3).

On unconditional backbone generation, PAR is evaluated against FrameDiff, RFDiffusion, ESM3, Genie2, and Proteina using designability, FPSD/fS, diversity, novelty, and secondary-structure metrics (Table 1).
PAR demonstrates zero-shot generalization to human-prompted conditional generation and motif scaffolding without fine-tuning (Section 4.2).
Combining SDE and ODE sampling across scales yields a 2.5x inference speedup over the single-scale 400-step baseline (Table 2).

71154.text: The paper presents an end-to-end framework for systematic rare-event analysis of probabilistic LLM outputs (Section 1).
The implementation covers theory, efficient rare-completion generation strategies, probability estimation, and error analysis (Section 2).
The paper analyzes rare completions in TinyStories models for ARI and log-probability observables (Section 4).
The paper uses trajectory path sampling and MBAR-style reweighting to estimate rare-event probabilities and diagnose overlap between biased distributions (Figure 6).

71077.text: RoboMME benchmarks long-horizon, history-dependent VLA manipulation tasks requiring temporal, spatial, object, and procedural memory (Figure 1).
The benchmark comprises 16 manipulation tasks organized under the four memory categories (Section 3).
RoboMME includes 770K high-quality training timesteps for systematic evaluation of memory-augmented policies (Section 3).
The paper builds 14 memory-augmented VLA variants on the pi0.5 backbone to compare memory representations and integration strategies (Section 4).
Experiments show memory representation effectiveness is highly task-dependent, with different designs excelling on different memory demands (Section 5).

71029.text: Feature Activation Coverage measures post-training data diversity in an interpretable LLM feature space rather than using only text-level diversity metrics (Section 3).
FAC Synthesis uses sparse autoencoders to identify missing features in a seed dataset and generate synthetic samples that activate those features (Section 4).
The paper reports consistent diversity and downstream-performance improvements on instruction following, toxicity detection, reward modeling, and behavior steering (Section 5).
Using 100% of selected missing features outperforms lower selected-feature ratios across the four downstream tasks in the reported ablation (Table 7).
The paper identifies a shared interpretable feature space across LLaMA, Mistral, and Qwen that enables cross-model knowledge transfer (Section 6).

71153.text: The paper introduces the ME^2 principle to characterize reasoning quality along macro/micro and efficiency/effectiveness dimensions (Section 3).
Reasoning traces are modeled as directed acyclic graphs to support pairwise evaluation of complex reasoning structures (Section 4).
The DAG-based evaluation pipeline is used to construct the TRM-Preference dataset and train a Thinking Reward Model for scalable reasoning-quality evaluation (Section 5).
At test time, selecting better reasoning traces yields up to 19.3% performance gain (Section 6).
During RL training, thinking rewards improve reasoning and task performance by up to 3.9% across diverse tasks (Section 6).

UGAP2F6FfV.text: Holi-Spatial is a fully automated pipeline for constructing large-scale spatially aware multimodal data directly from raw video inputs without human intervention (Section 3).

Holi-Spatial supports multi-level spatial supervision including optimized 3DGS reconstructions, rendered depth maps, object-level annotations, relational annotations, and spatial QA pairs (Section 3).
Holi-Spatial-4M contains 12K optimized 3DGS scenes, 1.3M 2D masks, 320K 3D bounding boxes, 320K instance captions, 1.2M 3D grounding instances, and 1.2M spatial QA pairs (Section 4).
Holi-Spatial outperforms existing feed-forward and per-scene optimized methods on ScanNet, ScanNet++, and DL3DV data-curation quality benchmarks (Section 5).
Fine-tuning VLMs on Holi-Spatial-4M improves 3D grounding and spatial reasoning performance (Section 5).

lJpXXwhRRF.text: Vision2Web spans static UI-to-code generation, interactive multi-page frontend reproduction, and long-horizon full-stack website development (Section 2).
The benchmark contains 193 real-world website-development tasks across 16 categories, with 918 prototype images and 1,255 test cases (Table 2).
Task complexity increases from static webpages to interactive frontends and full-stack websites in prototype images, test cases, and text-token requirements (Table 2).
The evaluation protocol combines a GUI agent verifier with a VLM-based judge in a workflow-based agent verification paradigm (Section 3).

Evaluations of multiple VLMs under different coding-agent frameworks reveal substantial performance gaps at all task levels, with state-of-the-art models still struggling on full-stack development (Section 4).

WwS8CTpUA6.text: SceneSmith generates simulation-ready indoor environments from natural-language prompts through hierarchical stages from architectural layout to furniture and small-object population (Section 3).
Each generation stage is implemented as an interaction among VLM agents with designer, critic, and orchestrator roles (Section 3).
SceneSmith integrates text-to-3D synthesis for static objects, dataset retrieval for articulated objects, and physical-property estimation (Section 3).
Across 210 room- and house-level prompts, SceneSmith generates 3-6x more objects than prior methods, with under 2% inter-object collisions and 96% physics-stable objects (Section 4).
In a 205-participant user study, SceneSmith achieves 92.2% average realism and 91.5% prompt-faithfulness win rates against baselines (Table 1).
SceneSmith scenes are used in an end-to-end pipeline for automatic robot policy evaluation without manual environment or success-predicate design (Section 5).

7UEBX1KU1y.text: The paper proves DPO-RLHF equivalence is conditional on the RLHF-optimal policy preferring human-preferred responses (Section 3).
When the equivalence assumption fails, DPO optimizes relative advantage over the reference policy rather than absolute human-preference alignment (Section 3).
The paper characterizes undesirable solution spaces in which policies reduce DPO loss while preferring dispreferred responses (Section 3).
Constrained Preference Optimization augments RLHF with constraints and derives a stationary DPO-like loss with an adaptive reference-based margin (Section 4.3).
The paper gives a soft-margin ranking interpretation showing DPO can implement margin ranking with potentially negative targets (Section 5).
Experiments on standard benchmarks report state-of-the-art performance for CPO (Section 6).

9kJQjx2B80.text: ProcMEM/Skill-Pro learns reusable procedural skills from interaction experience without updating model parameters (Section 3).
The Skill-MDP formalism converts passive episodic narratives into executable skills with activation, execution, and termination conditions (Section 3).
Non-Parametric PPO uses semantic gradients for candidate skill generation and a PPO Gate for robust skill verification (Section 4).
Skill-Pro achieves higher reuse rates than baselines in in-domain, cross-task, and cross-agent evaluations (Table 1).
Skill-Pro maintains only 816 memory tokens while achieving the highest reported ALFWorld success rate of 0.90 under extreme compression (Table 2).
Ablations evaluate the contribution of skill use, online score, and PPO Gate pass rate to Skill-Pro performance (Table 3).

ePFvXPdvhM.text: PACT is a post-training framework that projects pretrained diffusion policies onto constraint-feasible regions without demonstration data or task rewards (Section 3).
PACT distills constraint gradients into the diffusion model through a reverse-KL objective with dense supervision across denoising timesteps (Section 3).
PACT uses a curriculum that progressively tightens constraints while theoretically maintaining bounded policy shift and monotone improvement (Corollary 3.4).
On simulated and real-world embodied manipulation benchmarks, PACT reduces safety violations by 31.0% on average while improving task success by 30.7% (Section 4).

PAR combines multi-scale downsampling, an autoregressive transformer for conditional embeddings, and a flow-based backbone decoder (Figure 1).
PAR addresses autoregressive exposure bias with noisy context learning and scheduled sampling (Section 3).

On unconditional backbone generation, PAR is evaluated against FrameDiff, RFDiffusion, ESM3, Genie2, and Proteina using designability, FPSD/fS, diversity, novelty, and secondary-structure metrics (Table 1).
PAR demonstrates zero-shot generalization to human-prompted conditional generation and motif scaffolding without fine-tuning (Section 4.2).
Combining SDE and ODE sampling across scales yields a 2.5x inference speedup over the single-scale 400-step baseline (Table 2).

zAl9heLw4q.text: Motive computes motion-specific data attribution by applying motion-weighted loss masks so gradients emphasize dynamic regions rather than static appearance (Section 3.4).
The method includes a video-specific frame-length bias fix to reduce spurious attribution to longer clips (Section 3.3).
Fine-tuning on Motive-selected data improves VBench motion smoothness and dynamic degree over baselines while using only a fraction of the training data (Table 1).
Human evaluation reports a 74.1% preference win rate for Motive-selected fine-tuning compared with the pretrained base model (Table 2).

eXxFlOPTk4.text: VideoKR contains 315K video reasoning examples over 145K newly collected CC-licensed expert-domain videos (Section 3.1).
The data pipeline uses human-curated seed examples, skill-oriented generation, and filtering intended to remove examples solvable from text or a few frames (Sections 3.3-3.5).
VideoKR-Eval is constructed to reduce single-frame shortcut answerability found in existing knowledge-intensive video benchmarks (Table 2).
SFT plus RL post-training on VideoKR improves knowledge-intensive video reasoning averages for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B compared with their base models (Table 3).
Ablations indicate that adding knowledge-enhanced perception and complex reasoning examples improves VideoKR-Eval and knowledge-intensive benchmark performance (Table 4).

t73XUJvyQr.text: LLapDiff models irregular targets as low-dimensional latent trajectories, enabling horizon-wide generation without numerical integration over physical time (Section 4.4).
The denoiser parameterizes mean evolution in the Laplace domain with stable complex-conjugate poles for direct evaluation at irregular timestamps (Section 4.2).
A renewal-averaging analysis maps irregular sampling gaps to effective event-domain poles and motivates gap-aware history conditioning (Section 4.3).
Across seven real-world datasets, LLapDiff reports the strongest long-horizon probabilistic forecasting results on the main CRPS/MSE comparison (Table 1).
The same queried latent-trajectory model performs missing-value imputation by querying historical timestamps without retraining (Figure 3).

3BW15kSPfN.text: h1 synthesizes long-horizon reasoning examples by chaining existing short-horizon GSM8K-style problems without new human or teacher-model annotations (Section 3).
The training recipe uses outcome-only RL with a curriculum that automatically increases composed problem horizon length (Section 3).
Curriculum RL on composed sixth-grade math problems boosts accuracy on GSM-Symbolic, MATH-500, and AIME by up to 2.06x (Table 1).
Models trained with h1 transfer to out-of-distribution ReasoningGym domains and long-context benchmarks (Table 2).
The analysis claims curriculum RL gives an exponential sample-complexity improvement over full-horizon training in a simplified long-horizon skills model (Section 6).

pZNo1YWT5x.text: XDLM unifies masked and uniform-noise discrete diffusion through a stationary noise kernel that recovers MDLM and UDLM as limiting cases (Section 3.1).
An algebraic scalar reformulation of posterior and KL terms reduces memory and computation for large-vocabulary XDLM training (Section 3.2).
XDLM surpasses UDLM by 5.4 points on averaged zero-shot language benchmarks after OpenWebText training (Table 1).
In few-step conditional image generation, XDLM reduces FID from MDLM's 80.8 to 54.1 at 4 steps (Table 3).
When applied to an 8B LLaDA model, LLaDA-XDLM reaches 15.0 MBPP at 32 sampling steps, more than doubling the base LLaDA score (Table 16).

mWxEAgz3xu.text: The study surveys 306 practitioners and conducts 20 in-depth production-agent case-study interviews across 26 domains (Section 3).
For deployed agents, 68% execute at most ten autonomous steps before requiring human intervention (Figure 8).
Seventy percent of the detailed production case studies rely on off-the-shelf models without SFT or RL weight tuning (Figure 6).
Human-in-the-loop evaluation is the dominant evaluation mode for deployed agents, used by 74.2% of surveyed deployed systems (Figure 10).
Reliability is identified as the top development challenge for production agents, ahead of latency and security constraints (Figure 11).

lK2o9OjoXf.text: Plantain trains models to interleave planning, private reasoning, and visible answers instead of using a think-then-answer format (Section 3).
The first visible intermediate response in Plantain is an explicit step-by-step plan intended to allow early user feedback (Section 3).
Plantain reports about a 6% pass@1 improvement across the evaluated math reasoning and coding benchmarks (Table 1).
Plantain reduces time-to-first-response by over 60% relative to think-then-answer baselines while preserving final-answer quality trends (Table 1).
Ablations compare plan-first interleaving against other interleaving strategies and report plan-first as the strongest configuration (Table 3).

Ws8swqL5ob.text: PhotoAgent formulates autonomous image editing as long-horizon decision-making with tree search, memory, visual feedback, and closed-loop execution (Section 3).
UGC-Edit contains 7,000 real user photos annotated with human aesthetic scores and is used to train an aesthetic reward model (Section 5.1).
The end-to-end editing benchmark contains 1,017 real-world photographs across portraits, landscapes, urban scenes, food, objects, and low-light imagery (Section 5.2).
PhotoAgent reports state-of-the-art results across quantitative metrics, qualitative assessment, and user studies on the 1,017-photo benchmark (Table 2).
Ablations attribute performance gains to exploratory long-horizon planning for multi-round aesthetic optimization (Section 5.4).

hCAEcqig2C.text: The paper formalizes randomized self-reduction learning and provides sample-complexity analysis under correlated sampling (Section 4).
RSR-Bench contains 80 benchmark functions for evaluating randomized self-reduction discovery (Section 5).
Vanilla Bitween discovers randomized self-reductions for 43 of 80 RSR-Bench functions, including the first known sigmoid reduction (Table 1).
Agentic Bitween discovers randomized self-reductions for 64 of 80 RSR-Bench functions by letting LLM agents propose query functions beyond the fixed prior query set (Table 1).
On nonlinear invariant benchmarks, the regression backend outperforms the MILP backend in sample count and runtime (Table 2).

fdkSA4F0lN.text: Weak diffusion priors can match strong-prior inverse-problem baselines when measurements are highly informative, such as many observed pixels (Table 1).
The theory gives conditions under which high-dimensional measurements make the Bayesian posterior concentrate near the true signal despite weak priors (Theorem 3.1).
Local-correlation analysis argues that weak and stronger natural-image priors can share spatial structure useful for reconstruction (Table 2).
Cross-domain experiments evaluate weak priors from domain mismatch and low-fidelity generators across inverse-problem tasks (Section 4.2).
The paper identifies failure regimes for weak priors, including box inpainting and large-scale super-resolution where strong priors remain important (Figure 3).

7pQIzVNctu.text: Rex converts explicit Runge-Kutta and stochastic Runge-Kutta schemes into algebraically reversible exponential solvers for diffusion ODEs and SDEs (Section 3).
The ODE Rex construction inherits arbitrary order of convergence and a non-zero linear stability region from the base McCallum-Foster method (Theorem A.1).
Rex achieves near-machine-precision reconstruction under exact inversion in image-generation inversion experiments (Figure 7).
Rex improves or remains competitive on unconditional generation, text-conditioned generation, and image editing benchmarks versus prior reversible solvers (Figures 7-9).
Rex enables accurate likelihood-based Boltzmann sampling on tri-alanine with flow models (Table 1).

EeuLO2BjFN.text: MaxRL defines a compute-indexed family of sample-based objectives that interpolates between standard RL and exact maximum likelihood as sampling compute increases (Abstract).
The MaxRL objectives admit a simple unbiased policy-gradient estimator for non-differentiable sampling settings (Abstract).
The paper claims MaxRL converges to maximum-likelihood optimization in the infinite-compute limit (Abstract).
Empirically, MaxRL Pareto-dominates tested existing methods across all evaluated models and tasks (Abstract).
MaxRL reports up to 20x test-time scaling efficiency gains compared with a GRPO-trained counterpart (Abstract).

h7WBYYJF1Q.text: The paper connects recurrent-depth language models to diffusion language models and uses this connection to motivate a diffusion forcing sampler (Section 3).
The sampler decodes new tokens every forward pass while refining latent states for those tokens in parallel through recurrent depth (Section 3.1).
The paper proves the sampler is strictly more expressive than baseline autoregressive generation under the same time budget on modern hardware (Theorem 4.2).
The diffusion forcing sampler applies directly to existing 3.5B recurrent-depth transformers without tuning (Section 5).
Experiments report around 5x generation speedups with roughly 1% quality trade-offs depending on task and hyperparameters (Table 1).

kR4iOTaAOJ.text: ThunderAgent abstracts agentic workflows as LLM Programs that unify KV cache, system state, and external tool resources (Section 3).
The system adds a program-aware scheduler to improve KV cache hit rates and reduce memory imbalance across agent workflows (Section 4.2).
The tool resource manager asynchronously prepares and reuses tool environments, including disk and port resources (Section 4.3).
ThunderAgent reports 1.5-3.6x serving throughput improvements over state-of-the-art inference systems (Figure 5).
ThunderAgent reports 1.8-3.9x RL rollout speedups and up to 4.2x disk memory savings (Figures 6 and 9).

PnTXyTR2VG.text: LatentLM represents continuous modalities with VAE latents and uses next-token diffusion for autoregressive generation of those latent vectors (Section 2).
The proposed sigma-VAE is designed to prevent variance collapse in continuous latent tokenization for autoregressive modeling (Section 2.3).
On ImageNet image generation, LatentLM reports competitive or better FID than Diffusion Transformer baselines with stronger scaling trends (Table 1 and Figure 4).
In multimodal large-language-model experiments, LatentLM outperforms vector-quantized models and Transfusion on scaling curves for text-to-image and image-to-text generation (Figure 8).
For zero-shot text-to-speech on LibriSpeech test-clean, LatentLM outperforms VALL-E 2 in speaker similarity and robustness while using far fewer autoregressive decoding steps (Table 4).

PeFSCRulgy.text: TerminalTraj filters repositories to construct Dockerized execution environments, generates Docker-aligned task instances, and synthesizes executable validated terminal trajectories (Abstract).
TerminalTraj curates 32K Docker images and generates 50,733 verified terminal trajectories across eight domains (Abstract).
Models trained on TerminalTraj with a Qwen2.5-Coder backbone report gains up to 20% on TerminalBench 1.0 and 10% on TerminalBench 2.0 over their backbones (Abstract).
TerminalTraj-32B reaches 35.30% on TB 1.0 and 22.00% on TB 2.0 among models with fewer than 100B parameters (Abstract).
The paper claims TerminalTraj-32B improves test-time scaling behavior on terminal-agent benchmarks (Abstract).

vTp9JToZl9.text: The paper identifies Cross-Modal Entropy Collapse as a failure mode caused by hard projection of sparse point clouds onto image-plane grids (Section 1).
SplAttN replaces hard projection with Differentiable Gaussian Splatting to create a dense continuous image-plane representation for 2D-3D fusion (Section 3.3).
SplAttN achieves state-of-the-art average Chamfer Distance on the PCN point-cloud completion benchmark (Table 1).
SplAttN reports best F1 score and lowest average Chamfer Distance on ShapeNet-34/21 seen and unseen splits (Table 3).
KITTI counterfactual evaluation shows SplAttN remains dependent on visual cues while baselines behave like unimodal template retrievers (Figure 8).

3gCdh3u2GK.text: Mind-Omni unifies seven brain, image, and text encoding/decoding tasks in a single discrete diffusion framework (Table 1).
The Brain Tokenizer converts continuous fMRI signals into discrete tokens aligned with image and text representations in a shared semantic space (Section 3.1).
The framework curates a Brain Question Answering instruction-tuning dataset using Qwen2-VL to support reasoning over brain signals (Section 4).
Mind-Omni establishes a new state of the art among unified brain-vision-language frameworks in the multi-task evaluation (Tables 2-4).
Joint image-text conditioning shows synergistic gains over single-modality conditioning in neural encoding and decoding analyses (Figures 7 and 8).

lwOoBzJykL.text: LaST0 represents future visual dynamics, 3D structure, and robot proprioceptive states as a token-efficient latent spatio-temporal chain of thought (Section 3).
The architecture uses a Mixture-of-Transformers design with a low-frequency reasoning expert and a high-frequency acting expert (Section 3.4).
LaST0 achieves a 98.1% mean success rate on LIBERO, reported as state of the art for that benchmark (Table 3).
Across real-world tabletop, mobile, and dexterous hand manipulation tasks, LaST0 improves mean success rates by 13%, 14%, and 14% over prior VLA methods (Table 5).
LaST0 reports a 14x inference speedup over explicit chain-of-thought VLA approaches (Section 1).

71122.text: RACO directly applies conflict-averse gradient descent to objective-specific pairwise preference losses instead of relying on explicit reward models (Section 3).
The clipped CAGrad update is introduced to stabilize multi-objective LLM alignment while respecting user-specified objective weights (Section 3.2).
The paper proves convergence of clipped CAGrad to Pareto-critical points that respect user-specified weights in nonconvex smooth settings (Theorem 3.1).
For two objectives, the analysis shows clipping can strictly improve the convergence rate (Theorem 3.2).
Experiments on multi-objective summarization and safety alignment across Qwen 3, Llama 3, and Gemma 3 report better Pareto trade-offs than reward-free baselines (Section 4).

F9NDKf5oPy.text: The paper formalizes masked diffusion sampling as an MDP in which the diffusion language model is the environment and the policy chooses which tokens to unmask (Section 3).
The learned unmasking policy is a lightweight single-layer transformer mapping token confidences to unmasking decisions (Section 3.2).
Policy sampling matches state-of-the-art heuristic samplers in semi-autoregressive block generation settings (Figure 4).
Learned policies outperform heuristic unmasking strategies in the full-diffusion generation setting (Figure 5).
Visualization of learned full-diffusion policies shows expert-steered policies recovering a left-to-right unmasking order on GSM8K samples (Figure 7).

XFTTezxLdU.text: Pretraining on Dyck sequences raises context-recall needle-in-a-haystack accuracy from 10% to 98% in the diagnostic experiments (Figure 2).
Front-loading 0.1% to 0.3% procedural data before natural-language, code, or math pretraining significantly outperforms standard pretraining (Figure 7).
Procedural pretraining lets models reach the same loss using 55%, 67%, and 86% of the original data on C4, CodeParrot, and DeepMind-Math respectively (Table 1).
Mechanistic transfer experiments find procedural pretraining affects attention and MLP layers differently across code and language domains (Section 6).
Experiments study combinations of multiple procedural-data forms as a path toward broader warm-start pretraining (Section 7).

fXr3uPr1G5.text: The paper proposes a unified QAT scaling law modeling quantization error as a function of model size, training data volume, and quantization group size (Section 3).
The scaling law is fit and evaluated using 268 W4A4 QAT experiments consuming 276K A100 GPU-hours (Section 4.1).
Quantization error decreases with model size but increases with more training tokens and coarser quantization granularity in the W4A4 setting (Figure 1).
Weight and activation quantization errors follow the overall W4A4 trend but have different sensitivities to training token count (Figure 5).
Activation quantization error in the FC2 layer caused by outliers is identified as the primary W4A4 QAT bottleneck, and mixed precision reduces that bottleneck (Figure 7).

Efq2VvYk1o.text: ThreadWeaver introduces a two-stage parallel trajectory generator for producing parallel chain-of-thought data for supervised fine-tuning (Abstract).
ThreadWeaver uses a trie-based rollout design to enable parallel reasoning on off-the-shelf autoregressive inference engines (Abstract).
The framework includes parallelization-aware reinforcement learning to balance reasoning accuracy with effective parallelization (Abstract).
On six math reasoning benchmarks, ThreadWeaver trained on Qwen3-8B reaches 79.9% on AIME24 and 71.9% average performance (Abstract).
ThreadWeaver reports up to 1.53x token-latency speedup while matching comparably sized sequential reasoning models (Abstract).

09CSjVeDug.text: DMPO fine-tunes diffusion LLMs by matching the model policy distribution to an optimal reward-tilted distribution through cross-entropy optimization (Section 3).
The method introduces weight baseline subtraction to make small-batch DMPO training effective (Section 3.4).
DMPO is trained without supervised fine-tuning in an R1-Zero-like recipe for reasoning tasks (Section 4).
Across evaluated reasoning benchmarks, DMPO consistently outperforms LLaDA-Instruct, LLaDA-1.5, d1, and cGRPO baselines (Table 1).
DMPO reports accuracy gains up to 54.3% over previous state-of-the-art baselines and 66.41% over the base model (Table 1).

ENuMNYCiV6.text: The paper proposes a meta-cognitive knowledge augmentation framework with Cognition-Guided Knowledge Expansion and Cognition-Driven Knowledge Calibration modules (Figure 2).
It reports a structural decay law linking higher answer accuracy to lower uncertainty across QA tasks and model families (Figure 1, Figure 7).
The full framework outperforms compared knowledge-augmentation and calibration baselines on diverse QA benchmarks (Table 1).
Ablations attribute performance gains to the proposed meta-cognitive assessment, knowledge expansion, and calibration components (Table 2).
CDKC improves confidence calibration and aligns subjective certainty with objective correctness across evaluated datasets (Figure 5, Figure 6).

Targeted deletion or augmentation of high-influence samples causally modulates induction-head and previous-token-head emergence more than random interventions (Figure 2).
High-influence samples for induction heads are concentrated in repetitive structural domains, with top-ranked examples including LaTeX, HTML, and repeated text patterns (Table 1, Figure 4).
Synthetic data patterns selected from Pythia-14M attribution generalize to larger model scales when augmenting induction-head formation (Table 2).
Interventions that alter induction-head strength also shift in-context learning scores, supporting a causal link between the mechanism and ICL behavior (Figure 5).

LcswwEzzX7.text: AugE-Toolkit segments a source robot, inpaints the background, replays the trajectory with a target robot in simulation, and composites the augmented robot into the scene (Figure 1).
Scaling the number of augmented robot embodiments improves robustness on the source Franka robot under lighting and occlusion perturbations (Figure 2).
Simulation experiments evaluate how adding more augmented robots affects transfer to augmented robots and generalization to unseen robots (Figure 3).
OXE-AugE is built from selected OXE and additional datasets and expands the source demonstrations into millions of augmented trajectories (Figure 7).
Fine-tuning OpenVLA and pi0 on augmented Bridge data improves physical-task success on tested robot-gripper embodiments versus original Bridge-only training (Figure 4).

coHiGZOFtS.text: VenusBench-Mobile defines 149 primary tasks across 10 user-intent categories and 27 apps, plus 80 environment-variation tasks for stability testing (Figure 1, Figure 4).
The benchmark introduces the PUDAM taxonomy, scoring mobile GUI agents along Perception, Understanding, Decision, Action, and Memory dimensions (Figure 5, Table 6).
Its evaluation infrastructure combines Android-emulator interaction with hybrid verification using MLLM-as-a-judge and programmatic checks (Figure 6).
Evaluated mobile GUI agents show substantially lower success rates on VenusBench-Mobile than on AndroidWorld, exposing harder user-centric tasks (Figure 2, Table 3).
Stability evaluation requires success across original, Chinese, dark-mode, pad, and min/max setting variants, and reports low stability pass rates for agents (Table 4).

Hm8OEDKpiO.text: The OrthoMind-3D dataset combines programmatically generated in-domain scenes with out-of-domain game-engine and generative-AI scenes for block counting and object reasoning (Figure 2, Figure 6).
3ViewSense trains models in two stages: inducing canonical front/left/top orthographic views and then performing view-grounded reasoning with optional RL refinement (Figure 3).
On OrthoMind-3D, 3ViewSense improves block-counting and object-reasoning accuracy over evaluated VLM baselines (Table 1).
The method generalizes to out-of-domain OrthoMind-3D scenes and external spatial benchmarks better than the Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct base model (Table 2).
Ablations show that supervising view-grounded reasoning and using the two-stage SFT design outperform direct QA or incomplete training variants (Table 4, Table 5).

vKWxArobP3.text: AGSM formulates text-image alignment rewards with Plackett-Luce modeling and incorporates alignment guidance into score matching (Section 3.1, Section 3.2).
The method uses positive and negative soft tokens to adjust diffusion noise predictions toward aligned pairs and away from negative pairs (Figure 2, Algorithm 1).
AGSM improves T2I generation metrics on SD1.5, SDXL, and SD3 across COCO-val 5K and GenEval compared with baseline and SoftREPA variants (Table 1).
AGSM remains stable in later-stage training while SoftREPA validation ImageReward degrades despite lower training loss (Figure 4).
AGSM improves text-guided image editing trade-offs between alignment and structural preservation across PnP, MasaCtrl, and RF-Inversion settings (Table 2, Figure 5).

2hQBG2ZlFb.text: The paper categorizes SFT objectives by their token-probability gradient weights and positions them along a model capability continuum (Section 3, Figure 2, Figure 3).
At the model-strong end, prior-leaning objectives such as -p and thresholded NLL outperform standard NLL across the main evaluated models and datasets (Table 1).
At the model-intermediate region, prior-leaning and NLL objectives produce similar performance (Table 2).
At the model-weak end, NLL consistently outperforms the prior-leaning -p objective (Table 3).
Quantile-thresholding analysis finds low-probability tokens are harmful for model-strong settings but useful for model-weak settings (Figure 5).

KRSZj8z5Lr.text: LiME shares a single PEFT adapter and applies lightweight expert-specific modulation vectors instead of replicating a full adapter per expert (Figure 1).
LiME combines zero-parameter routing, adaptive expert selection, n-gram routing granularity, PEFT compatibility, and a shared trainable PEFT module (Table 1).
Average benchmark results report LiME variants as competitive with or better than MoE-PEFT baselines while using fewer total trainable parameters (Table 2).
Efficiency experiments show LiME variants achieve higher throughput, shorter training time, and up to 4x fewer trainable parameters than corresponding MoE-PEFT methods (Figure 2).
LiME's expert modulation is theoretically bounded as an approximation to expert-specific PEFT, and CKA analysis reports similar representations to MoELoRA (Theorem 2, Table 3).

A5venxSvpw.text: MASPOB constructs agent topology and prompt embeddings, predicts performance with a GNN surrogate, and selects prompts with a Linear-UCB exploration bonus (Figure 1, Algorithm 1).
Coordinate-ascent search decomposes multi-agent prompt optimization and is compared against exhaustive global search for accuracy and runtime (Section 3.3, Table 6, Figure 4).
Across HotpotQA, DROP, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, and MATH, MASPOB reports the best or near-best mean accuracy among compared prompt-optimization methods (Table 1, Figure 2).
Replacing the GNN with an MLP reduces performance, supporting the role of topology-aware modeling in MASPOB (Table 3).
MASPOB generalizes to Qwen-3-32B as the backbone LLM under the same optimization settings (Table 4).

giNBsVVFGt.text: PRISM decomposes mid-training decisions across retention, domain interaction, benchmark selection, RL compatibility, and scaling behavior (Section 1).
PRISM mid-training improves code, math, and science benchmark averages across multiple model families compared with base checkpoints (Section Domain-wise Effects of Mid-Training Data).

Long-context restoration uses a base/mid-trained linear merge followed by long-context extension to recover RULER performance after mid-training degradation (Section Restoring Long-Context Ability After Mid-Training).
Weight analysis finds mid-training densely restructures model weights whereas RL makes sparse refinements (Section Weight-Level Analysis: Dense Restructuring vs. Sparse Refinement).

Applying RL after PRISM mid-training yields stable gains on code, math, and GPQA-Diamond benchmarks, while RL on base models shows limited progress on harder math benchmarks (Section Effects of Reinforcement Learning on Mid-Trained Models).

vSzRJyg6k0.text: RACO is an offline, reward-free preference-alignment method that accepts user-specified objective weights and explicitly handles conflicting objectives (Table 1).
The method uses CAGrad-Clip to limit correction gradients so updates better respect preferred objective trade-offs (Figure 1, Algorithm 1).
On TL;DR summarization, RACO achieves better Pareto frontiers for conciseness-quality and faithfulness-quality trade-offs than AMoPO and weighted-loss DPO baselines (Figure 2, Figure 3).
On BeaverTails safety alignment, RACO improves harmlessness-helpfulness Pareto trade-offs across Qwen3 and Gemma3 setups (Figure 4).
Ablations show clipping and the correction-radius constant affect validation margins and Pareto frontiers (Figure 5, Figure 6).

The MME-VLA suite evaluates symbolic, perceptual, and recurrent memory representations with multiple memory-integration mechanisms on a pi0.5-based architecture (Figure 2, Appendix A).
Main benchmark results show memory representation effectiveness is task-dependent across RoboMME task suites (Table 3, Figure 3).
Efficiency-performance analysis compares memory-augmented policies against baselines across success and resource metrics (Figure 4).
The benchmark includes real-world experiments in addition to simulated RoboMME evaluations (Table 4).

MCTS-discovered execution programs improve DART-Math accuracy under depth budgets and often solve inputs with shorter unique layer depth than standard inference (Figure 3, Figure 4).
PoLar trains an end-to-end network to predict execution programs, avoiding expensive sequential MCTS at inference time (Figure 2, Section 3).
On LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct, PoLar improves pass@k over standard inference and dynamic-depth baselines across DART-Math difficulty levels (Table 2).
PoLar reports out-of-distribution pass@1 gains on Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B-Chat (Table 3).

The tokenizer uses temporal interleaving, register tokens, causal attention, and nested dropout to induce a 2D temporal/coarse-to-fine representation (Figure 3).
On Kinetics-600 class-to-video generation, VideoFlexTok is compared against 3D grid tokenizers on reconstruction FVD, generation FVD, and classification-score alignment (Table 1).
Flexible-length generation maintains comparable or better fidelity while using fewer tokens and improving conditional alignment on class-to-video and text-to-video tasks (Figure 7).
VideoFlexTok demonstrates 10-second, 81-frame text-to-video generation using 672 tokens (Figure 8).

VMsumctGvg.text: The paper compares image-based and action-based latent-action perspectives with four VLA supervision strategies: LA-Align, LA-Direct, LA-Cond, and LA-Tok (Figure 1, Figure 3).
On LIBERO, latent-action supervision strategies are evaluated against a unified VLA baseline and prior methods using success rate (Table 1).
On RoboTwin 2.0, the paper reports success-rate differences between the baseline and each latent-action supervision strategy (Table 2).
Real-world manipulation experiments compare model scores on four tasks with 10 rollouts per model-task (Figure 4, Table 3).
Ablations compare continuous embedding versus discrete-token latent-action supervision (Table 4).

The method instantiates a practical alternating decoder with an exact subset-update step inside a candidate-pool loop (Section 4.2).
Top-W is evaluated against Min-p, Top-p, and Top-H on GSM8K across multiple temperatures and models (Table 1).
Top-W is evaluated against the same decoding baselines on GPQA across multiple temperatures and models (Table 2).
Judge-based open-ended evaluations report Top-W wins on more AlpacaEval and MT-Bench temperature-model tuples than the compared decoding methods (Figure 1, Figure 2).

Training and propagation analyses show unconstrained HC has larger loss gaps, gradient norms, and residual propagation instability than mHC (Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 5, Figure 7).
The paper introduces kernel fusion, recomputing, and communication-overlap infrastructure to reduce mHC system overhead (Section 4.3, Table 2, Table 3, Figure 4).
At 27B scale, mHC outperforms the baseline and surpasses HC on most zero-shot and few-shot downstream benchmarks (Table 4).

Solution density and diversity around Qwen2.5 instruction-tuned models increase with model scale (Figure 3).
Randomly sampled perturbations exhibit diverse task specialties rather than all acting as generalists (Figure 4).

RandOpt samples random parameter perturbations, selects top performers, and ensembles predictions; it matches or exceeds PPO, GRPO, ES, and related baselines in many LLM post-training settings (Algorithm 1, Figure 6).
RandOpt accuracy improves with population size and depends on sufficient pretrained model scale (Figure 7, Figure 8).

The Explorable Sphere-Aware DiT block combines exploration-aware attention for route control with sphere-aware attention for spherical geometric adjacency (Figure 2).
Quantitative evaluation compares PanoWorld-X with panoramic video generation and camera-controllable generation models (Table 1).
Qualitative comparisons show improved detail clarity and geometric coherence across generated panoramic keyframes (Figure 3).
Ablations evaluate the contribution of individual framework components (Table 2, Figure 5).

FneePKFVHT.text: PaperBanana is an agentic framework for generating academic methodology diagrams and statistical plots from source context and communicative intent (Figure 1, Figure 2).
PaperBananaBench contains 292 methodology-diagram test samples with source-context and caption statistics reported by the authors (Figure 3).
On PaperBananaBench, PaperBanana outperforms leading baselines on faithfulness, conciseness, readability, aesthetics, and overall score (Table 1).
Ablation studies evaluate the contribution of individual agent components to PaperBananaBench performance (Table 2).
For statistical plots, the paper compares vanilla Gemini-3-Pro, PaperBanana, code-based visualization, and image-generation approaches (Figure 4, Figure 5).

Parallel training uses Jacobi iteration to update latent hidden states in parallel rather than naively unrolling sequential latent thoughts (Figure 3, Section 3.2).
Scaling curves report that PonderLM-2-Pythia matches larger Pythia baselines with fewer parameters or fewer training tokens on the 300B Pile (Figure 1).
PonderLM-2-Pythia achieves lower language-modeling perplexity than same-size Pythia and larger vanilla Pythia baselines (Figure 4).
Zero-shot and five-shot downstream evaluations show average accuracy gains over corresponding Pythia baselines (Table 2).

jPKqiaPTEd.text: TEDBench is a large-scale non-redundant protein fold classification benchmark built from TED/AFDB predicted structures with an external experimental-structure test set (Figure 1, Table 1).

Masked Invariant Autoencoders mask a high ratio of backbone frames, encode only unmasked frames with an SE(3)-invariant geometric encoder, and reconstruct full-frame targets with a decoder (Figure 3).
MiAE benchmark results on TEDBench outperform or compete with supervised and pretrained protein-structure models across accuracy and macro-F1 metrics (Table 2).
Linear probing results isolate MiAE representation quality against models with more than 1B parameters (Table 3).

Ablations show high masking ratios, decoder design, reconstruction losses, masking strategy, model scale, and sequence incorporation affect TEDBench linear-probe performance (Figure 4, Figure 5, Table 5).

Annealed transition path sampling generates biased text-completion trajectories that explore rare high- or low-observable completions (Figure 1, Figure 2, Algorithm 2).
MBAR reweighting reconstructs the true distribution of observables such as automated readability index from biased simulations (Figure 3).
Error analysis compares confidence intervals for MBAR rare-event estimates against direct sampling estimates (Figure 4).
Biasing toward readability uncovers rare completions far beyond the training-data quantiles and correlates with token repetition behavior (Figure 5).

The WIRE transformation is equivariant to node-order permutations up to sign flips and rotations in degenerate eigenspaces (Lemma 1).
Regular RoPE is recovered as a special case of WIRE on grid graphs with appropriate learnable frequencies (Theorem 2, Figure 2).
WIRE asymptotically depends on graph effective resistance under the paper's spectral-feature assumptions (Theorem 3).

Experiments report WIRE improvements on synthetic monochromatic-subgraph and shortest-path tasks, point-cloud transformers, and efficient graph transformer benchmarks (Table 1, Table 2, Table 3, Table 4).

The method uses skill-centered datasets whose examples require the new skill composed with existing pretrained skills (Section 3.3, Figure 2).
Skill neologisms are compared with fine-tuning, LoRA, prompt tuning, and related approaches for skill-based continual learning properties (Table 1).
On digit-sequence transformation tasks, independently learned skill neologisms transfer to held-out two-skill and three-skill compositions (Table 3, Table 4, Figure 4, Figure A2).
Zero-shot composition of independently trained SHIFT and INV-POL skill tokens outperforms or complements in-context learning baselines in the reported setup (Figure 5).
A natural-language Skill-Mix experiment shows two separately learned skill neologisms can be combined at inference to elicit both target skills (Figure 7).
