TokSuite includes a multilingual robustness benchmark with 4,941 total examples across English, Chinese, Turkish, Italian, Farsi, Math, and STEM perturbation groups (Table 7).

The paper reports tokenizer-dependent relative performance drops under multilingual perturbations including input-medium, diacritic, orthographic, morphology, noise, LaTeX, STEM, and math perturbations (Table 1).
All 14 models converge to similar bits-per-byte values without loss spikes, supporting comparison of downstream differences as tokenizer effects rather than failed training (Figure 6).

2UH01A9Za0.text: DiReCT formulates annealing-stage sample selection as constrained optimization over per-sample gradients using Hessian spectral properties (Section 4.2).
The method imposes directional constraints so selected samples align with a curvature-aware descent path during LLM annealing (Section 4.4).
The flat-direction preference theorem states that the surrogate objective increases along sufficiently flat Hessian eigendirections under the paper's spectral regularity assumptions (Theorem 4.4).
DiReCT attains the highest aggregate annealing score among tested data-selection baselines at both GPT-2-Medium 355M and Llama-1.1B scales (Table 4).
DiReCT prioritizes high-loss, long-sequence samples under the paper's high-loss and short-length probing regimes (Figure 3).

OC2z7iSQKa.text: tau2-bench introduces a telecom dual-control environment where both the conversational agent and simulated user can act with tools in a shared dynamic state (Figure 1).
The telecom domain is modeled with separate agent and user databases, 13 agent tools, 30 user tools, and 114 sampled tasks from a 2,285-task full set (Table 1).
The benchmark uses a compositional task generator that creates verifiable telecom tasks from intent and subtask components (Section 3.2).
Agents show lower pass@1 in default dual-control telecom operation than in no-user and oracle-plan modes, isolating the cost of decentralized user coordination (Figure 4).
Telecom performance declines as the number of required actions or distinct issues increases (Figure 5).

BhahZSDowo.text: Critique-Resilient Benchmarking evaluates answers by treating an answer as correct unless an adversarial critique is upheld under bounded verification (Section 3.2).
The protocol admits generated questions through feasibility gating that rejects questions whose self-answer is successfully critiqued or whose question is ill-posed (Figure 1).
The ranking model jointly estimates answerer, questioner, and item effects with an itemized bipartite Bradley-Terry model (Section 5.2).
Answerer Elo scores correlate more strongly with external benchmark means than a baserate predictor in the reported Spearman and Kendall analyses (Table 1).
Train-set scores predict unseen question outcomes better than a baserate predictor in pooled log-loss and Brier score metrics (Table 2).

hgMZraPlSv.text: The paper formulates formal problem-solving as a deterministic Markov decision process and implements FPS inside formal theorem proving environments (Section 3.1).
Deductive Formal Problem-Solving decouples forward answer construction from optional backward proof validation for find-all problems (Figure 2).
FPS soundness is proved: any direct answer produced by FPS satisfies the formal problem predicate (Theorem 3.6).
D-FPS completeness and soundness for find-all problems are stated as formal theorems under the paper's conditions (Theorems 3.8 and 3.9).
The benchmark suite consists of FormalMath500, MiniF2F-Solving, and PutnamBench-Solving, constructed from informal and theorem-proving math benchmarks (Section 4.2).
The strongest evaluated baselines solve at most 23.77% of FormalMath500, 27.47% of MiniF2F-Solving, and 0.31% of PutnamBench-Solving (Table 1).

The synthetic analysis shows post-training selection almost surely fails to recover optimal lower-rank submodels from arbitrary global low-rank minimizers (Theorem 4.1).
Nested subspace learning preserves nested minimizers for every rank in the synthetic matrix setting (Theorem 4.3).
FlexRank shows more graceful accuracy degradation than compared low-rank elastic baselines across LLM and ViT parameter budgets (Figure 4).
FlexRank submodels can be further fine-tuned with LoRA for math and code domains at multiple elastic sizes (Table 1).
Gauge-Aligned Reparametrization converts active-rank selection into measured forward-pass speedups on an RTX 5090 GPU (Figure 10).

Object-level replacement in embedding space preserves intended probing and retrieval behavior for counterfactual scene edits (Table 3).
CLIP's binding function is high-complexity: approximators recover concept recognition on held-out objects but perform poorly on object recognition (Figure 4).
Controlled transformer embedding models trained from scratch achieve binding generalization on entirely held-out objects when training coverage is sufficiently high (Figure 6).
Multiplicative concept-interaction probes explain held-out-object binding better than additive probes in the controlled models (Figure 8).

syG9I9ofd8.text: LatentMAS replaces text-mediated multi-agent communication with auto-regressive latent thought generation and a shared latent working memory (Figure 3).
The paper proves latent thoughts can be more expressive than equivalent text reasoning under a linear representation hypothesis (Theorem 3.1).
Latent working memory preserves information equivalently to directly inputting preceding agents' outputs under the paper's formal setup (Theorem 3.3).
LatentMAS reports higher accuracy, lower output token usage, and faster inference than single-agent and text-based MAS baselines across six general tasks in the sequential MAS setting (Table 1).
On AIME, GPQA-Diamond, and other reasoning-intensive tasks, LatentMAS is evaluated under both sequential and hierarchical MAS settings with accuracy, token, and speed metrics (Table 2).
Input-output alignment improves downstream accuracy by 2.3% to 5.3% across three analyzed benchmarks (Figure 7).

yKcBAJMPXZ.text: MetaphorVU-Bench defines eight video-metaphor categories for systematic metaphorical video understanding evaluation (Figure 2).
The benchmark construction pipeline filters real-world short videos through multi-stage automatic filtration and manual annotation with quality control (Figure 3).
Current MLLMs perform far below a human-written upper bound on MetaphorVU-Bench, while reasoning-enhanced baselines provide limited improvement (Table 2).
Manual error analysis attributes MLLM failures mainly to missing, superficial, or improper cross-domain metaphor mapping rather than only wrong recognition (Table 3).
MetaphorBoost augments inference with a metaphorical knowledge graph and improves average scores for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking, and Gemini-3-Pro (Table 2).
Ablations show external metaphor-oriented graph knowledge is more effective than no external augmentation, plain text knowledge, or commonsense graph substitution (Table 4).

5PfEQzE9bf.text: The paper studies midtraining as distributional bridging that mixes specialized data with general pretraining data before supervised fine-tuning (Figure 1).
Controlled experiments pretrain Pythia-family models from 70M to 1B parameters on C4 for a fixed 128B-token budget before midtraining and SFT evaluation (Section 3.1).
Code-focused midtraining yields the largest gains on code tasks, math-focused midtraining improves math tasks, and mismatched midtraining provides little benefit (Table 2).
Proximity advantage between midtraining and target SFT data correlates with midtraining performance improvements across dataset pairs (Figure 3).
Midtraining mixtures outperform continued pretraining on 100% specialized data for tested code and math settings while preserving lower C4 validation loss (Table 3).
For code midtraining, early specialized-data introduction supports high mixture weights, while late introduction makes high mixture weights detrimental (Figure 4).

m1IRWFAMsa.text: NorMuon combines Muon's orthogonalized updates with neuron-wise adaptive normalization based on second-order momentum statistics (Algorithm 1).
The optimizer analysis shows Muon lowers update condition numbers but leaves high variance in per-neuron update norms, while NorMuon normalizes neuron contributions (Figure 1).
NorMuon achieves 21.74% better step efficiency than Adam and 11.31% improvement over Muon on the 1.1B pretraining setting (Table 1).
NorMuon also improves validation-loss trajectories over Muon and AdamW at the 5.4B scale (Figure 2).
On 5.4B training, NorMuon keeps optimizer-state memory close to Muon and below AdamW, with about 2.9% total training-step time overhead over AdamW (Table 2).
NorMuon outperforms Muon in Modded-NanoGPT pretraining at 124M and 350M parameter scales (Figure 5).

06Nk3dJDMq.text: The paper derives prompt steering interventions by subtracting unsteered activations from prompt-steered activations and trains PSR models to approximate successful prompt interventions (Figure 1).
Prompt steering applies highly token-dependent intervention strengths, motivating token-specific activation steering rather than constant coefficients (Figure 2).
PSR models estimate token-specific steering coefficients from activations and are trained with log-likelihood or MSE objectives to imitate prompt steering (Sections 3.4 and 3.5).
On Persona Vectors, all-layer PSR models outperform prompt steering at prompt-steering coherence for all three reported language models (Table 1).
On AxBench Gemma layer subsets, PSR variants improve over several rank-1 activation steering baselines and compare with multi-rank or multi-layer methods (Table 3).
Accumulated PSR interventions have lower relative RMSE to prompt-steering interventions than constant steering on the analyzed Persona Vectors data (Figure 3).

ds3ZOevkwx.text: MADQA contains 2,250 human-authored questions grounded in 800 heterogeneous PDF documents (Abstract).
The corpus spans 12.2M tokens across domains including financial, reports, government/regulatory, legal, HR, reference, and technical documents (Table 2).
MADQA is designed to include visual, structured-layout, tabular, and artifact-dependent questions rather than text-only document QA (Figure 4).
Agentic systems outperform static RAG baselines on MADQA, but an 18% oracle gap remains, indicating retrieval is a major bottleneck (Table 3).
Frontier BM25 MLLM agents can match human accuracy only at high step limits, while humans achieve much higher first-query accuracy (Figure 9).
Human searchers remain better calibrated across effort levels than MLLM agents under the Kuiper effort-accuracy calibration analysis (Figure 10).

RNuC8Nj6rD.text: TD3B formulates allosteric binder design as control over sequence-conditioned transition operators rather than optimization toward static conformations (Section 4.2).
The framework combines a target-aware Direction Oracle, a soft binding-affinity gate, and amortized fine-tuning of a masked discrete diffusion model (Figure 2).
The Direction Oracle achieves 0.93 accuracy, 0.90 precision, 0.91 recall, and 0.90 F1 for binary direction classification (Table 1).
TD3B obtains the highest gated reward among compared pre-trained, classifier guidance, SMC, TDS, and PepTune baselines (Table 2).
For targeted transition control, generated binders achieve 61% success for forward transitions and 100% success for reverse transitions under the paper's success definition (Table 3).
The paper evaluates TD3B-designed agonist and antagonist binders on GLP-1R and OX1R case studies (Figures 4 and 5).

GnqHK8Ww98.text: SOAR trains a teacher model with meta-RL to generate synthetic problems rewarded by measured improvement in a student model on hard target problems (Section 3.2).
The experiments target sparse-reward math subsets where the base model has 0/128 initial success on sampled hard problems (Abstract).
Students trained on SOAR promotion questions outperform hard-only training and intrinsic-reward teacher baselines on MATH and HARP fail@128 evaluations (Figure 3).
Grounded teacher rewards yield more stable student pass@32 trajectories than intrinsic teacher rewards across teacher seeds (Figure 4).
SOAR-generated MATH promotion questions recover 75% of the gains from full MATH training, while HARP promotion questions recover 50% of the gains from full HARP training (Section 5).
The final trained teacher policy does not improve direct inference on fail@128 test problems, separating generator utility from solver ability (Section 5).

kcyOjXoUZu.text: WALRUS is pretrained on 19 continuum-dynamics scenarios spanning astrophysics, geoscience, rheology, plasma physics, acoustics, and classical fluids (Abstract).
Patch jittering is theoretically motivated as a way to cancel aliasing artifacts in expectation under the paper's frequency-domain model (Proposition 3.1).
The training pipeline embeds 2D data into a combined 2D-3D space using singleton dimensions, zero padding, and symmetry-preserving augmentations (Figure 2).
Load-balanced distributed training buckets token counts to reduce deadweight in heterogeneous 2D/3D workloads (Figure 3).
After fine-tuning, WALRUS outperforms prior physical-dynamics foundation models on average one-step, short-horizon, and medium-horizon VRMSE metrics across downstream tasks (Figure 4).
The paper reports WALRUS achieves state-of-the-art results on 56 of 65 metrics across 26 tasks (Section 5.2).

IMFgiWw4jd.text: The ME2 principle characterizes reasoning traces along macro/micro granularity and efficiency/effectiveness axes (Figure 2).
The paper represents reasoning traces as DAGs with progression, branching, and merging structures for pairwise evaluation (Figure 3).
TRM is trained from a TRM-Preference dataset with a Bradley-Terry preference loss to score reasoning trace quality at scale (Section 5.1).
TRM reaches 88.6% accuracy on the validation-set pairwise preference evaluation, outperforming Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B, ReasonFlux-PRM-7B, and prompt-only judging (Table 1).
TRM-guided best-of-N test-time selection improves AIME24 and AIME25 performance over compared PRM baselines for GPT-OSS-20B and Qwen3-8B response models (Figure 4).
TRM-guided RL improves STEM and math benchmark averages over verifier-only RL, with the largest reported gains on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Table 2).

BkMSFFtm5M.text: CVE-Factory transforms sparse CVE metadata into executable agentic vulnerability tasks containing instructions, environments, and verification tests (Figure 1).
The multi-agent pipeline uses six decoupling and coupling stages coordinated by an orchestrator with verification-triggered feedback (Figure 2).
Cross-validation against PatchEval reports 95.35% solution correctness and 96.13% environment fidelity pass rates (Table 1).
LiveCVEBench contains 190 tasks across 14 programming languages and uses more multi-container environments than Terminal-Bench or PatchEval (Table 2).
Fine-tuning Qwen3-32B on CVE-Factory tasks improves LiveCVEBench performance from 5.29% to 31.05% and Terminal-Bench from 12.50% to 31.25% (Table 3).
CVE-Factory achieves a 90.3% success rate in the workflow ablation, outperforming CVE-Genie at 48.4% and a Claude Code single-agent baseline at 0.0% (Table 4).

The sheaf diffusion operator is presented as a drop-in generalization of the diffusion operation used in graph convolutional networks (Section 2.1).
On synthetic semi-supervised node-classification tasks over signed graphs, sheaf neural networks outperform Kipf-Welling GCN variants across feature and edge-noise regimes (Figure 1).
The experiments average results over five random graph trials and report standard-deviation error bars for SheafNN and GCN comparisons (Figure 1).

wsA8LgHU5U.text: Learning-to-Theorize trains models to infer executable, compositional latent programs from raw observation pairs without direct program supervision (Figure 1).
Neural Theorizer infers a latent program by iteratively selecting primitives with a theory programmer and executing them through a shared transition model (Figure 2).
An MDL criterion selects the shortest accurate executable explanation among candidate program lengths at test time (Section 3.3).
On GridWorld, NEO and search-augmented NEO-S generalize to compositional and length-OOD settings where monolithic discrete and continuous baselines largely fail (Table 1).
On Arithmetic Factorization Reasoning, NEO-S substantially improves compositional-OOD and length-OOD transfer over monolithic baselines (Table 2).
Grounding loss, codebook size, and MDL weight each materially affect primitive recovery and OOD performance in the GridWorld ablation (Table 3).

iJwDylm93H.text: GUI-RobustEval contains 1,216 executable test cases targeting policy-induced GUI-agent error recovery (Table 1).
The benchmark evaluates recovery across four controllable error depths and reports both post-error success and error-awareness metrics (Table 2).
RoTS synthesizes error-recovery trajectories through explore-recovery co-expansion with fragility-driven exploration and experience-informed recovery (Figure 2).
RoTS-32B achieves 47.4% OSWorld success at max steps >=50 and 33.8% All-Pass@4, reported as state-of-the-art among compared GUI agents (Table 3).
Adding both fragility-driven exploration and experience-informed recovery improves GUI-RobustEval awareness/post-error success and OSWorld All-Pass@4 over parallel sampling alone (Table 4).
Scaling expansion rounds and dataset size improves RoTS success rate in the reported synthesis scaling analysis (Figure 5).

97NEP1pyS3.text: RLER maintains a fixed-size rubric buffer that is updated with rubrics generated from current rollouts and pruned by rollout-score variance (Figure 2).
DR Tulu-8B is trained as an open long-form deep-research agent using supervised cold start followed by online RL with asynchronous tool calls (Sections 4.2 and 4.3).
Across ScholarQA-CSv2, HealthBench, ResearchQA, and DeepResearchBench, DR Tulu-8B RL averages 65.6 and exceeds the best prior open baseline by 15.6 points (Table 1).
DR Tulu-8B lies on the performance-cost Pareto frontier and is reported as about 1000x cheaper per ScholarQA-CSv2 query than OpenAI Deep Research (Figure 1).
Evolving rubrics outperform using only initial search-based rubrics during RL training, with the gap widening over training (Figure 6).
Using Qwen3-8B as both judge and rubric generator still improves over the SFT baseline, though it underperforms GPT-based judging by 1.3 points (Table 4).

UamxHbDR3p.text: The paper formalizes text-driven amodal 3D generation, where text prompts steer unseen-region completion while preserving the observed input (Section 1).
RelaxFlow is a training-free dual-branch framework with an observation branch and a semantic-prior branch fused by velocity blending (Figure 3).
The relaxation mechanism is theoretically linked to low-pass filtering that reduces semantic vector-field estimation error (Proposition A.4).
The paper introduces ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D diagnostic benchmarks for evaluating extreme occlusion and semantic ambiguity in amodal 3D generation (Section 5).
RelaxFlow improves CLIP image/text scores, FID, LPIPS, and Point-FID over its TRELLIS and SAM3D backbones on ExtremeOcc-3D (Table 1).
RelaxFlow obtains the highest automatic CLIP scores and user-study preferences for alignment, 3D fidelity, and overall preference on AmbiSem-3D (Table 2).

The framework uses exploration assessment to trigger off-policy rubric-guided refinement only when on-policy exploration is insufficient (Figure 2).
RGR-GRPO improves over the verifiable online RL baseline by average margins of +7.0% on mathematics, +5.4% on physics, +8.4% on chemistry, and +6.6% on general reasoning benchmarks (Table 1).
The method is evaluated across 14 benchmarks spanning mathematics, physics, chemistry, and general reasoning domains (Section 3).
Ablations show rubric categories, off-policy shaping, and exploration assessment each contribute to average performance (Table 2).
The paper proves exploration assessment acts as a necessary adaptive variance controller for stabilizing RGR-GRPO training under its analysis assumptions (Theorem C.1).

7MlfE2Da2W.text: SCALE jointly modulates visual attention temperature and action decoding temperature using the VLA model's self-uncertainty (Figure 2).
The method requires no additional training, no verifier, and only a single forward pass per control step (Section 3.3).
With an OpenVLA backbone on LIBERO, SCALE improves average success rate over greedy decoding and compared sampling, top-k, top-p, and TTS baselines (Table 1).
With a pi0-FAST backbone on LIBERO, SCALE improves average success from 91.2% to 93.0% over the fine-tuned greedy baseline (Table 2).
On SIMPLER-WidowX, SCALE improves average success for pi0-FAST from 34.4% to 49.0% and improves SpatialVLA fine-tuned and zero-shot settings (Table 3).
Real-world pick-and-place experiments show SCALE improves average in-distribution and out-of-distribution success for both OpenVLA and pi0-FAST backbones (Table 5).

ATpOQt9VVd.text: OeMDM defines a generalized masked-diffusion NELBO that decomposes into a reconstruction term and a velocity-mismatch term for order-aware generation processes (Proposition 3.2).
OeMDM recovers autoregressive left-to-right modeling as a special case under a suitable scheduler (Proposition 3.3).
LoMDM jointly trains the diffusion backbone and learnable order schedulers from scratch with a single objective rather than post-training an unmasking sampler (Section 4.1).
LoMDM reports lower test perplexity than prior discrete diffusion baselines on LM1B and OpenWebText (Table 1).
LoMDM reports better zero-shot perplexity than MDLM on all seven evaluated transfer datasets and best diffusion results on most of them (Table 2).
The learned LoMDM scheduler improves generative perplexity relative to MDLM and to no-scheduler ablations across tested NFE budgets (Table 3).

Motion-aware submap construction uses optical flow to prune static redundancy and preserve turning segments for stable local geometry (Section 3.1).
VGGT-Motion improves KITTI absolute trajectory error over VGGT-Long and other foundation-model SLAM baselines under the paper's calibration-free setting (Table 1).
On long-sequence 4Seasons, Complex Urban, and A2D2 benchmarks, VGGT-Motion reports much lower ATE and drift than VGGT-SLAM and VGGT-Long while other foundation-model baselines often fail (Table 3).
Topology-aware turning encapsulation outperforms temporal slicing and parallax-triggered partitioning on KITTI ATE and drift (Table 5).
The runtime study reports large total-time speedups over VGGT-Long and VGGT-SLAM on long-sequence benchmarks (Figure 5).

ncRRCG4BfP.text: WestWorld introduces a knowledge-encoded embedding module and a system-aware mixture-of-experts block for trajectory world modeling across robot morphologies (Figure 1).
The model is pretrained on 89 complex environments spanning simulated and real-world robot data (Section 5).
WestWorld reports the best zero-shot long-horizon trajectory prediction errors against MLPEnsemble, TDM, and TrajWorld on Walker2D, Hopper, and Franka-style systems (Table 1).
WestWorld reports lower few-shot MAE and MSE than baselines on Cassie, A1, and UR5, averaged over three random seeds (Table 2).
Using WestWorld as the MPPI dynamics model improves accumulated reward on Walker2D, Hopper, and Unitree Go1 control tasks compared with evaluated baselines (Table 3).
Ablations attribute zero-shot gains to both the system-aware MoE layer and structural embeddings (Table 4).

fSnxuRhWoC.text: EOSTok jointly optimizes a 1D tokenizer and autoregressive generator so generation losses can supervise tokenizer learning end to end (Section 3).
The Autoregressive Prediction Reconstruction loss decodes teacher-forced AR predictions into pixel space to improve AR-predictable latent representations (Section 3).
EOSTok-H reports a guidance-free FID of 1.48 on ImageNet-1K 256x256 generation (Table 3).
EOSTok-L reports 1.74 guidance-free gFID with 312M parameters and 0.73 reconstruction FID for its tokenizer (Table 3).
Ablations report that semantic vision-foundation-model alignment improves 1D tokenizer convergence and reconstruction quality (Table 2).
Ordering and sequence-length ablations show that original 1D token order and moderate sequence lengths are important for generation quality (Tables 4 and 5).

Mkal0hTCnh.text: MEnvAgent uses a Planning-Execution-Verification multi-agent loop plus environment reuse via retrieval and incremental patching of historical environments (Figure 2).
MEnvBench contains 1,000 tasks from 200 repositories across 10 programming languages with execution support, quality assurance, and domain diversity (Table 1).
Across Kimi-K2 and Gemini-3-Flash backbones, MEnvAgent improves average F2P by 8.6 points, PASS by 11.0 points, and reduces time by 43.0% versus SWE-Factory (Table 2).
Removing EnvPatchAgent or environment reuse lowers reuse/pass rates and increases runtime in component ablations (Table 3).
Fine-tuning open-source coding models on MEnvData-SWE trajectories improves resolved rates on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-bench Multilingual (Table 4).
MEnvData-SWE contains 3,005 task instances and 3,872 solution trajectories across 942 repositories and 10 languages (Table 12).

The method adds Noisy Gradient Pruning to filter uninformative reward differences under noisy red-teaming rewards (Section 4).
The Min-K Fluency Stabilizer penalizes non-fluent out-of-distribution prompts to reduce gibberish reward hacking (Section 4).
Stable-GFN reports stronger attack diversity and attack performance than GFN baselines across LLM red-teaming settings (Section 5).
Ablations evaluate loss-function and reward-stabilization choices, including the effect of reward constraints on attack discovery (Table 3).

WJcFtJriqv.text: UDM-GRPO treats the final clean sample as the policy action and reconstructs training trajectories with the diffusion forward process to stabilize GRPO for uniform discrete diffusion (Section 4.2).
Reduced-Step training optimizes three early high-noise timesteps to accelerate convergence (Section 4.3).
CFG-Free training removes classifier-free guidance during RL training while recovering and surpassing CFG-based quality after optimization (Section 4.4).
UDM-GRPO raises URSA GenEval overall score from 0.69 to 0.96 and reports state-of-the-art GenEval results among compared continuous and discrete T2I models (Table 1).
UDM-GRPO reports GenEval 0.96, PickScore 23.81, and OCR 0.57, improving over URSA and URSA without CFG (Table 2).
Ablations show final-clean-sample actions and forward-process trajectories outperform backward-trajectory variants on GenEval, PickScore, and OCR (Table 3).

8VVbElV06v.text: UniPercept-Bench organizes perceptual image understanding into Image Aesthetics, Image Quality, and Image Structure & Texture domains with Domain-Category-Criterion hierarchy (Figure 1).
UniPercept-Bench supports both Visual Rating and Visual Question Answering tasks for perceptual-level evaluation (Section 3.2).
UniPercept is trained with Domain-Adaptive Pre-Training followed by Task-Aligned RL for Visual Rating and VQA (Figure 6).
UniPercept outperforms compared MLLMs on UniPercept-Bench Visual Rating tasks (Table 1).
UniPercept is evaluated as a plug-and-play reward model for text-to-image post-training to improve perceptual attributes of generated images (Section 5.3.2).
The appendix defines ISTA in detail and compares UniPercept-Bench with other perceptual benchmarks (Sections 8 and 9.3).

On LLaMA2-13B sequence lengths from 32K to 80K, AGoQ reports faster training than Megatron-LM and ZeRO-1 while avoiding activation recomputation in the listed settings (Table 2).
AGoQ reports lower memory than COAT and comparable or faster training time on OLMo-1B at 24K and 32K sequence lengths (Table 3).

ArBG reports improvements over flow-based Boltzmann generators across all evaluated molecular benchmarks, with especially large gains on 10-residue Chignolin (Section 4).
The paper introduces Robin, a 132M-parameter transferable ArBG model for molecular sampling (Section 4).
Robin reports more than a 60% reduction in zero-shot E-W2 energy error on 8-residue systems relative to the previous state of the art (Abstract).

MqzZ9X6m7f.text: The paper argues that compute efficiency alone is insufficient for sustainable open-source AI because lower per-run costs can increase aggregate derivative experimentation and deployment (Section 1).
The Data and Impact Accounting proposal standardizes carbon and water reporting metadata for model derivatives (Section 3).
DIA is designed as a lightweight transparency layer that integrates low-friction measurement into common training and inference pipelines (Section 3).
The position calls for public dashboards that aggregate impact reports across model releases and derivative lineages (Section 3).
The paper's central claim is that tracking only base-model impacts leaves cumulative open-source derivative footprints largely invisible (Abstract).

76XSBLdBdg.text: Hibiki-Zero trains simultaneous speech translation from sentence-level aligned speech data rather than word-level aligned interpretation data (Section 3).
Hibiki-Zero casts latency-quality optimization as reinforcement learning with GRPO over multistream speech/text outputs (Section 3.3).
The final Hibiki-Zero architecture is a 3B-parameter decoder-only multistream model built on RQ-Transformer audio token modeling (Section 4.1).
On Europarl-ST and Audio-NTREX-4L, Hibiki-Zero reports better long-form ASR BLEU, speaker similarity, and latency than Seamless, and improves over Hibiki on French short-form ASR BLEU (Table 1).
Human MOS evaluations rate Hibiki-Zero higher than Seamless on audio quality, speaker similarity, and speech naturalness across evaluated input languages (Table 2).
The model adapts to Italian-to-English simultaneous translation using 850 hours of fine-tuning data and reports Seamless-level quality/latency with better speaker similarity after RL (Table 3).

9wpwfSJCp9.text: SleepLM aligns multimodal polysomnography signals with natural language to support sleep interpretation and interaction beyond closed sleep-label spaces (Section 3).
The paper introduces a multilevel sleep caption generation pipeline for creating sleep-text supervision (Section 3).
The curated sleep-text dataset comprises more than 100K hours of data from over 10,000 individuals (Abstract).
SleepLM uses a unified pretraining objective combining contrastive alignment, caption generation, and signal reconstruction (Section 3).
SleepLM reports state-of-the-art performance on zero-shot and few-shot sleep understanding, cross-modal retrieval, and sleep captioning tasks (Section 4).
The paper demonstrates language-guided event localization, targeted sleep insight generation, and zero-shot generalization to unseen sleep tasks (Section 4).

gc7Gg18ejz.text: The paper proves tracking-error dynamics for a linear critic under non-stationary targets and connects stability to embedding covariance geometry (Theorem 3.1).
The analysis argues that isotropic representations equalize contraction directions and reduce drift amplification under a fixed variance budget (Section 3.1).
The paper motivates Gaussian representations because Gaussian higher-order moments are determined by covariance, limiting uncontrolled tail behavior (Section 3.1).
Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization shapes learned representations toward an isotropic Gaussian distribution during RL training (Section 4).
On non-stationary CIFAR-10, adding SIGReg improves train accuracy AUC, feature rank, and dormant-neuron metrics across Adam, RAdam, and Kron optimizers (Table 1).
The empirical study reports that SIGReg reduces representation collapse, neuron dormancy, and training instability across evaluated RL domains (Section 5).

XztRm216YS.text: TimeRewarder learns dense proxy rewards from action-free passive videos by predicting frame-wise temporal distances (Figure 2).
The method converts predicted progress differences between adjacent frames into step-wise rewards for downstream RL (Section 4.2).
The paper provides a theoretical justification connecting temporal distance to progress-based reward shaping (Section 4.3).
On held-out expert videos, TimeRewarder reports the highest Value-Order Correlation among evaluated progress-based reward baselines (Figure 3).
TimeRewarder distinguishes successful and failed rollouts more coherently than VIP, Rank2Reward, and PROGRESSOR in qualitative reward/value curves (Figure 4).
On ten Meta-World tasks, TimeRewarder reports nearly perfect success in 9 of 10 tasks with 200,000 environment interactions per task (Abstract).

gz7hVnrRWq.text: The paper identifies performance plateaus, ineffective spontaneous self-reflection, and persistent failures as limitations of RL with only numerical rewards (Section 3.1).
Critique-GRPO trains from both initial responses and critique-guided refinements while combining numerical rewards with natural-language critiques (Section 4).
Critique-GRPO with CoT critiques improves average Pass@1 over R1-GRPO and R1-Dr.GRPO on Qwen2.5-7B-Base and Qwen3-8B across eight reasoning tasks (Table 2).
On Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Base, Critique-GRPO reports a 21.6-point average Pass@1 gain using 4K RL prompts and outperforms numerical-feedback baselines using 46K prompts (Table 3).
Self-critique Critique-GRPO improves Qwen3-8B average Pass@1 to 68.13 and AIME24 Avg@32 to 60.00 (Table 4).
Fine-grained ablations attribute gains to KL removal, language feedback, refinement sampling, and policy shaping, with the full objective reaching 47.08 average Pass@1 on Qwen2.5-7B-Base (Table 6).

z1bSFIEexL.text: Visual Information Gain is defined as a perplexity-based log-ratio measuring how much image conditioning reduces answer uncertainty (Section 3.2).
VIG is decomposable to sample and token levels, enabling fine-grained detection of visually grounded tokens such as colors, spatial relations, and attributes (Section 3.3).
Examples on MS-COCO show VIG is positive for matching images, smaller for partially grounded images, and negative for conflicting images (Table 1).
Token-level analysis identifies high positive loss differences for visually grounded words and near-zero or negative differences for weakly visual tokens (Table 2).
VIG-guided selective training prioritizes high-VIG samples and tokens to improve visual grounding while reducing supervision (Section 3.4).
Experiments compare VIG-guided selective training against full-data and existing methods for overall performance, data efficiency, and language-bias mitigation (Sections 4.2 and 4.3).

bYDjZyqKxq.text: MEMO optimizes inference-time context for multi-turn multi-agent LLM games by combining persistent memory retention with exploration through prompt evolution (Section 3).
The retention component stores structured insights from self-play trajectories in a memory bank and injects them as priors in later games (Section 3).
The exploration component uses tournament-style prompt evolution with TrueSkill-based uncertainty-aware selection and prioritized replay of rare or decisive states (Section 3).
Across five text-based games, MEMO raises GPT-4o-mini mean win rate from 25.1% to 49.5% and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct from 20.9% to 44.3% using 2,000 self-play games per task (Abstract).
MEMO reduces run-to-run variance and yields more stable rankings across prompt variations (Abstract).
MEMO reports its largest gains in negotiation and imperfect-information games, while RL remains stronger in perfect-information settings (Abstract).

qiZDlnvWTR.text: NanoQuant formulates post-training LLM quantization as low-rank binary factorization with binary matrices and learned scales (Section 3).
NanoQuant is the only compared PTQ method marked as supporting both 70B+ LLMs and sub-1-bit compression (Table 1).
Across Llama, Gemma, Qwen, and Rnj model families, NanoQuant reports functional WikiText-2 perplexity at 1-bit and sub-1-bit settings where naive binary methods often fail catastrophically (Table 2).
NanoQuant reports competitive zero-shot commonsense accuracy against higher-bit binary PTQ baselines on Llama-3 and Qwen3 models (Table 3).
NanoQuant compresses Llama-2-70B from 137.95GB to 5.75GB, enabling the 70B model to fit within an 8GB consumer GPU memory budget (Section 4.4).
Latent-binary ADMM initialization outperforms Dual-SVID and DBF ADMM initializations for 0.8-bit Rnj-1 compression (Table 5).

XQlUqVCHJd.text: TimeSpot defines a joint geo-temporal benchmark requiring structured prediction of four temporal and five geographic attributes from ground-level images (Section 3).
The dataset contains 1,455 ground-level photos from 80 countries with broad season, daylight, month, continent, climate, and environment coverage (Table 2).
TimeSpot includes hemisphere sanity, hard OOD, geo-temporal fusion, schema, calibration, and verifiable GPS/OSM-style scoring axes absent from many prior benchmarks (Table 1).
Evaluated VLMs show substantially weaker temporal understanding than coarse geolocation, with top time-of-day accuracy far below top country accuracy (Table 3).
The benchmark reports that the strongest VLMs can reach 77.59% country accuracy while still incurring a median geodesic error of 892.54 km and low time-of-day accuracy (Section 1).
Supervised fine-tuning improves TimeSpot performance but remains insufficient for robust physically grounded geo-temporal reasoning (Section 5.4).

HwXyyvK7ZJ.text: VLM-RobustBench evaluates 49 augmentations, including 42 severity-based corruptions across nine categories and 7 binary transforms (Table 1).
The benchmark yields 133 corrupted settings per model-dataset pair by applying three severities to 42 corruptions plus seven binary transforms (Section 3.2).
The evaluation covers 11 VLMs from Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5, Molmo2, and Gemma 3 families on MMBench and MMMU-Pro (Section 4.1).
Low-severity glass blur causes an average 8.1 percentage-point MMBench accuracy drop, larger than high-severity brightness reduction, illustrating a severity mismatch (Figure 1).
The study finds that spatial and resampling perturbations such as upsample and elastic_transform can cause drops up to 34 percentage points (Section 1).
Robustness is reported to vary by model family rather than simply by parameter count, producing family-specific vulnerability fingerprints (Section 1).

5kTn1c3vtt.text: Spectral Sphere Optimizer enforces module-wise spectral constraints on both weights and updates to realize a fully muP-aligned optimization process (Section 3).
SSO derives steepest-descent update directions on the spectral sphere and contrasts them with Muon and MuonSphere geometry (Figure 4).
SSO maintains constant activation magnitudes during Dense-1.7B training while AdamW produces substantially larger activation outliers (Figure 1).

On Dense 1.7B pretraining, Spectral Sphere reaches AdamW's final validation-loss level in 19% fewer steps and reports the highest average downstream accuracy among compared optimizers (Figure 8 and Table 3).
On MoE 8B-A1B training, Spectral Sphere reports the lowest validation loss and best expert load balance by MaxVio among compared optimizers (Figure 9).
On a 200-layer DeepNet stress test, Spectral Sphere attains lower loss and higher stability than AdamW and other spectral optimizers (Figure 10).

ldCiNVFt8O.text: d2 is a reinforcement-learning framework for masked diffusion language models built around estimating sampling-trajectory likelihoods (Section 3).
d2-AnyOrder provides exact trajectory likelihood with a single model pass for DLMs that support any-order decoding (Section 3).
The paper empirically shows that any-order decoding support is not universal across widely used DLMs (Section 4).
d2-StepMerge approximates trajectory likelihood for standard masked diffusion models with a tractable compute-accuracy tradeoff (Section 3).
d2 reports stronger performance than widely used RL baselines when applied to popular diffusion language models (Section 5).
d2 reports new state-of-the-art diffusion-language-model results on Countdown, Sudoku, GSM8K, and MATH500 reasoning benchmarks (Section 5).

QrC8OgQyOI.text: Prism performs Hierarchical Trajectory Search with stochastic exploration, progressive thinning, and final refinement for discrete diffusion language models (Algorithm 1).
Self-Verified Feedback ranks intermediate completions without loading an external verifier model during pruning (Section 3).
Local branching uses partial remasking to explore alternative completions while preserving high-confidence tokens (Algorithm 1).
Prism achieves comparable or better math/code accuracy than best-of-N decoding with substantially fewer denoising function evaluations on LLaDA 8B, Dream 7B, and LLaDA 2.0-mini (Table 1).
SVF calls are reported as sparse relative to denoising NFE, often below 10% of total NFE (Section 4.3).
Ablations show that removing SVF or remasking lowers GSM8K performance for LLaDA-8B across Prism target widths (Table 4).

r7uOjvZdzO.text: The paper decomposes VLM post-training into visual perception, textual reasoning, and visual reasoning stages with dedicated data for each capability (Section 1).
Its error analysis attributes 86.9% of sampled incorrect Qwen3-VL-8B answers on three visual math datasets to visual perception errors (Section 1).
Staged Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B models outperform their base counterparts on overall visual math and perception benchmark averages (Table 1).
Staged training outperforms merged training on the same base VLMs, including a Qwen3-VL-8B overall average of 65.77 versus 64.67 (Table 2).
Stage-order ablations show that perception-first or perception-early curricula perform better than reversed order on visual math and perception metrics (Table 3).
Stage 1 reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards yields stronger perception and downstream visual math performance than caption-based supervised fine-tuning (Table 4).
